title: Cluster membership and high availability
scope:
This category covers how an MDS daemon lives inside an unmodified Ceph cluster and how a rank survives failures: the monitor-owned FSMap and per-file-system MDSMap (fields, epochs, encodings, subscriptions, client decoding), compat sets and upgrade gating, the MMDSBeacon protocol and liveness, standby selection, standby-replay, failover and OSD blocklist fencing, the monitor `fs`/`mds` commands that change or show membership, the rank state machine, and the recovery pipeline replay, resolve, reconnect, rejoin, clientreplay, active and stopping, plus the daemon process anatomy (messenger, MonClient subscriptions, threads, timers, `mds_lock`, dispatch). Sources are the fact-checked map pages fsmap-and-mdsmap, beacon-and-monitor, rank-lifecycle-and-recovery, resolve-and-rejoin and process-and-threading. Much of the behaviour in the first five groups is implemented by the unmodified MDSMonitor; those entries describe the contract an MDS daemon must live inside, not code the MDS runs.

Excluded and owned elsewhere: reconnect message encoding, session states, eviction and blocklisting of clients, `required_client_features`, `refuse_client_session` and session timeouts (02-client-sessions-and-protocol); completed-request bookkeeping and request forwarding semantics (04-namespace-and-posix-operations); cap and lock semantics referenced by rejoin (03-caps-leases-and-locking); journal event formats and OSD epoch barriers and blocklist checks (06-journal-and-storage); subtree migration and the balancer, including balancer settings and export targets in the MDSMap (07-multi-mds); snapshot flags, `MRemoveSnaps` and `allow_multimds_snaps` (08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes); quiesce membership and metrics pings (10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine); admin socket commands, the `status` output, perf counters, the meaning of individual health metrics, the health checks the monitor derives from the map, and configuration plumbing (11-security-admin-and-observability); file-lock recovery from reconnect messages (04-namespace-and-posix-operations). Background on what `mds_lock` protects is in [mds_lock-analysis](../cpp-map/00-architecture/mds_lock-analysis.md).

Cross-category review (2026-10-11): entries that duplicated an entry of the owning category were retired (listed under "retired" in features.json with the entry they were merged into) or shortened to pointers whose description starts with "See F-XXX-NNN." and keeps only the facts specific to this category.

features.name: FSMap: monitor-owned map of all file systems
features.summary: The Paxos-versioned cluster map that lists every file system, every known MDS daemon and the shared standby pool; read by mgr, tools, cephfs-mirror and libcephfs.
features.description: The FSMap holds every `Filesystem` (fscid, MDSMap, MirrorInfo), the shared standby pool (`standby_daemons`, `standby_epochs`), `mds_roles` (gid to fscid or NONE), `default_compat`, `legacy_client_fscid`, `enable_multiple`, `next_filesystem_id` and `btime`. Only the MDSMonitor on the leader monitor writes it: commands, beacons and the 5 s monitor tick mutate one pending map, which is committed as one FSMap epoch per Paxos proposal (delayed to `paxos_propose_interval` 1 s after the previous commit, or `paxos_min_wait` 0.05 s; immediate when a daemon is blocklisted). Encoding is struct v8, compat 6 (the decoder requires v7 or later); it is sent whole as `MFSMap` (type 45) to `fsmap` subscribers. The monitor store keeps up to `mon_max_mdsmap_epochs` (500) versions. MDS daemons influence the map only through `MMDSBeacon`, `MMDSLoadTargets` and two mon commands.
features.notes: `FSMap::operator=` does not copy `ever_enabled_multiple` or `struct_version`, and `PaxosFSMap::create_pending` uses it, so the pending map always carries the default `ever_enabled_multiple = true` (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, code reading). See also F-CLU-013 (mirroring metadata).

features.name: MDSMap: per-file-system map and its wire encoding
features.summary: The per-file-system projection of the FSMap that MDS daemons and every client decode to find ranks, their states and addresses, and the file system settings.
features.description: Fields: rank sets `in`, `up` (rank to gid), `failed`, `stopped`, `damaged`; `mds_info` (every holder and standby-replay follower as `mds_info_t` v10: global_id, name, rank, inc, state, state_seq, addrs, laggy_since, export_targets, mds_features, join_fscid, flags FROZEN=1, compat); flags; data and metadata pools; `session_timeout` (60), `session_autoclose` (300); `max_file_size`; `max_xattr_size`; `required_client_features`; balancer settings; standby settings; `qdb_cluster_leader/members`; `compat`; `fs_name`; `enabled`; `last_failure_osd_epoch`; `tableserver` and `root` (always 0). Native encoding is struct_v 5, compat 4, extended version 20, carried in `MMDSMap` (type 21, header v2: fsid, u32 epoch, length-prefixed map, always-empty `map_fs_name`); the map is re-encoded per connection for peers lacking PGID64, MDSENC, MSG_ADDR2 or SERVER_NAUTILUS (the kernel advertises all four). Flag bits: NOT_JOINABLE 1<<0, ALLOW_SNAPS 1<<1, ALLOW_MULTIMDS_SNAPS 1<<4, ALLOW_STANDBY_REPLAY 1<<5, REFUSE_CLIENT_SESSION 1<<6, REFUSE_STANDBY_FOR_ANOTHER_FS 1<<7, BALANCE_AUTOMATE 1<<8; default 0x12.
features.notes: `ever_allowed_features` is a `uint8_t` while BALANCE_AUTOMATE is bit 8, so that bit is silently dropped; `last_failure` and `cas_pool` are never written (fsmap-and-mdsmap sections 4.1 and 8). Settings owned elsewhere: session timeouts and `refuse_client_session`/`required_client_features` ([sessions](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/sessions.md)), `max_xattr_size` ([attributes-and-xattrs](../cpp-map/03-request-path/attributes-and-xattrs.md)), snapshot flags ([snapshots](../cpp-map/10-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes/snapshots.md)), balancer settings ([balancer-and-pinning](../cpp-map/08-multi-mds/balancer-and-pinning.md)), quiesce membership ([quiesce](../cpp-map/12-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine/quiesce.md)).

legacy_parts.note: Per-connection re-encoding in MMDSMap::encode_payload: MDSMap struct v2 for peers without PGID64; struct v3 with extended version 5 and the unversioned mds_info_t for peers without MDSENC; mds_info_t v7 carrying only the legacy address for peers without SERVER_NAUTILUS; the legacy entity_addr_t encoding for peers without MSG_ADDR2. Client subscribers receive the MDSMap from the monitor in MMDSMap, whose encode_payload re-encodes the map for a connection that lacks PGID64, MDSENC, MSG_ADDR2 or SERVER_NAUTILUS. The 7.3 kernel advertises all four and current libcephfs advertises CEPH_FEATURES_ALL, so both receive struct_v 5 / extended version 20 with mds_info_t v10. The newest peers that get a re-encoded map are upstream kernels up to v5.10 (SERVER_NAUTILUS was added in 5.11) and Ceph clients before 14.x; the CentOS Stream 8/9 samples advertise SERVER_NAUTILUS and MSG_ADDR2.

features.name: Epoch model: FSMap, MDSMap and standby epochs, null map
features.summary: The epoch rules that decide which map is newer, which epoch a beacon must carry and when a map is pushed to every client of a file system.
features.description: Each committed proposal creates FSMap epoch `last_committed + 1`; a file system's MDSMap epoch is set to the FSMap epoch only when that file system or one of its daemons is modified (`modify_filesystem`, `modify_daemon`, `promote`, `erase`, `stop`, ...), so it is sparse but monotonic; a standby's map epoch is its `standby_epochs[gid]` entry; the null map has epoch `UINT32_MAX`. The kernel client, libcephfs and the C++ MDS drop maps whose epoch is not newer than the current one. Every beacon that reaches `prepare_beacon` (state change, health change, laggy clear, `mds_join_fs` change) calls `modify_daemon`, bumping the MDSMap epoch and pushing a new map to every MDS and mounted client of that file system.
features.notes: `fs reset` leaves the new MDSMap at epoch 0, so subscribers see the reset map only after the next modification (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code). A health message whose text changes every tick (for example "Behind on trimming (130/128)") produces a new MDSMap epoch roughly every beacon interval (beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.name: Map subscriptions and the MDS view of mdsmap (null maps)
features.summary: How the monitor decides which map each subscriber gets: clients by fs name or id, MDS daemons by matching their session address vector against the map.
features.description: Subscriptions: `fsmap` (MFSMap: mgr, cephfs-mirror, offline tools, libcephfs one-time for tell), `fsmap.user` (MFSMapUser), `mdsmap` (client: the MDSMap of `legacy_client_fscid`), `mdsmap.<fscid>`; all need mon cap `mds r`; `check_sub` filters the FSMap by the session's allowed fs names and sends nothing while `sub->next > epoch`. An MDS-type session whose address vector equals some `mds_info_t::addrs` receives its file system's MDSMap if it is attached (holder or standby-replay), a null map containing only its own `mds_info` at `standby_epochs[gid]` if it is a standby, or an empty map at the FSMap epoch if unknown; a null map is a default-constructed MDSMap (empty compat that decodes as incompat 7, `enabled` false, `fs_name` "cephfs", no ranks). Beacons from gids not in the committed map (not booting), evicted daemons and a committed STOPPED get a null `MMDSMap` with epoch `UINT32_MAX`.
features.notes: Because the MDS view is keyed by address equality, the daemon must subscribe and beacon from the same messenger identity whose addresses the monitor recorded at boot (beacon-and-monitor section 3.17). A daemon that applied the `UINT32_MAX` null map without restarting would stall all later beacons in `PaxosService::dispatch` (beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.name: FSMapUser: file system name directory for clients
features.summary: A small map of (fscid, name) pairs that clients use to mount a file system by name before subscribing to its MDSMap.
features.description: FSMapUser (v1) contains `epoch`, `legacy_client_fscid` and a list of `fs_info_t{s32 cid, string name}`; it is sent as `MFSMapUser` (type 103) to `fsmap.user` subscribers. The kernel client subscribes to it when mounted with `mds_namespace=`, libcephfs when `client_fs` or an fs name is given (one-time); both then subscribe to `mdsmap.<fscid>`. The MDS does not use it.

features.name: Kernel client partial MDSMap decode
features.summary: What the Linux kernel client reads from the MDSMap and how it reacts to rank changes; it fixes which map facts reach kernel mounts.
features.description: The kernel reads epoch, flags (stored in an unused field `m_client_epoch`), root, session_timeout, session_autoclose, max_file_size, max_mds, and per `mds_info` the gid, rank, inc, state, address (msgr2 or legacy), laggy_since and export_targets; entries with a rank out of range or **state <= 0 are ignored**, so standby-replay followers and CREATING/STARTING holders are invisible and such a rank reads as state 0. It then reads data pools, `in` (which sets `possible_max_rank = size(in)`), `enabled`, `fs_name` (the decode fails and the mount is shut down if it differs from `mds_namespace`), the damaged count and (ev >= 18) `max_xattr_size`; reads past the end after the pools still return the partial map as success. `check_new_map` force-closes sessions of ranks `>= possible_max_rank`, restarts a session on an address change, sends a reconnect when a restarting rank reaches `>= RECONNECT`, kicks requests and cap flushes at `>= ACTIVE`, and uses export targets of laggy or reconnecting ranks.
features.notes: Kernel `required_client_features` skip mismatch: the kernel skips the field as "u32 n then n x u64" while it is encoded as "u32 byte length then bytes"; with a non-empty set the skip over-runs, the later `max_xattr_size` read fails (map still accepted, `m_max_xattr_size` 0, all setxattr synchronous) or reads garbage (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code, not runtime-verified). Ranks are array indices bounded by `size(in)`, so ranks must stay contiguous. See also F-PROTO-062 (client reactions to rank changes).

legacy_parts.note: Selection of the LEGACY (msgr1) address from each mds_info address vector, the 'legacy' alternative of 'address (msgr2 or legacy)'. For each mds_info entry with info_v >= 8 the kernel takes the first address of the type its messenger speaks: MSGR2 when an ms_mode option is set, LEGACY when none is. mount.ceph with the new device syntax adds ms_mode=prefer-crc, so the baseline kernel selects the msgr2 address. LEGACY selection happens only with ms_mode=legacy or the old mon:/path device syntax, where the kernel's built-in default is msgr1.

features.name: libcephfs map use and mount availability check
features.summary: How libcephfs, ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha decode and use the MDSMap, including the mount-time availability test.
features.description: libcephfs decodes the whole map with the C++ `MDSMap::decode` (unknown trailing fields are skipped via the struct length). `Client::mount` fails with EACCES before contacting any MDS when REFUSE_CLIENT_SESSION is set, and checks `is_cluster_available()` only when `require_mds` is set: ceph-fuse passes `fuse_require_active_mds` (default true), `ceph_mount` passes false; STUCK (any damaged rank, empty `in`, any laggy up rank, or no ACTIVE rank) fails the mount with `CEPH_FUSE_NO_MDS_UP`, TRANSIENT (epoch 0) waits. It also uses `max_mds` to recognise stopped ranks, `export_targets` to pre-open sessions, `session_timeout/3` for cap renewal, `session_autoclose` as the upper bound of `ceph_set_deleg_timeout` (EINVAL otherwise, used by Ganesha delegations), `max_file_size` for writes and truncates, and the data pools for statfs; `mds_command` skips laggy daemons.

features.name: FSMap filtering for file-system-restricted sessions
features.summary: The monitor hides file systems a session is not allowed to see from its subscriptions and read-only commands.
features.description: Before serving a subscription or a read-only `fs`/`mds` command, the monitor filters the FSMap by the session's allowed fs names (`FSMap::filter`); mutating `fs` commands check `fsname` write capability per file system (EPERM) and return ENOENT for unknown file systems except `fs rm`, `fs rename` and `fs swap`. `fs dump <epoch>` decodes a stored historical FSMap and is not filtered.
features.notes: `FSMap::filter` removes the `mds_roles` entries of standbys but keeps `standby_daemons`, so filtered maps are internally inconsistent for standbys (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8).

features.name: FSMap sanity invariants enforced by the monitor
features.summary: Assertions the monitor applies to every committed or decoded FSMap; they bound the states the monitor can ever publish.
features.description: `FSMap::sanity` checks, unless `mon_mds_skip_sanity`: `legacy_client_fscid` is NONE or an existing fs; every daemon in a fs has a rank, maps to that fs in `mds_roles` and is not a standby; a non-standby-replay daemon is the `up` holder of its rank and the rank is neither failed nor damaged; standby-replay daemons exist only with `allow_standby_replay` (pending maps); every daemon compat is writeable for the fs compat; the quiesce leader is a member and members are in `mds_info`; `up` is a subset of `in`; standbys are STANDBY, rank NONE, with a `standby_epochs` entry. A violation asserts on the leader monitor. Not checked: `up + failed + damaged == in`, `in` and `stopped` disjoint, epochs.
features.notes: Several command sequences reach monitor asserts or `std::terminate` by code reading: `fs compat add_incompat` while standby-replay daemons remain, `fs reset` with a standby-replay still attached, `mds set_state` on a standby gid, `mds rmfailed` followed by a shrink, `fs compat add_*` with id >= 64 (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code).

features.name: Multiple file systems: enable_multiple and the default file system
features.summary: Whether more than one file system may exist, and which one unqualified clients and rank-only roles resolve to.
features.description: `fs flag set enable_multiple <bool>` (default true) controls creation of a second file system. `legacy_client_fscid` (dumped as `default_fscid`) is set to the first file system committed or by `fs set-default` (alias `fs set_default`); unqualified `mdsmap` subscriptions receive that file system's map and a bare `<rank>` role parses only when it exists. `fs rm` of the default fs clears it without choosing another, after which unqualified subscribers receive nothing.

legacy_parts.note: The deprecated command alias `fs set_default`. `fs set_default` is an AliasHandler of `fs set-default` registered with FLAG(DEPRECATED); a grep of src/pybind/mgr, src/cephadm, src/tools and Rook's Go sources finds no use of it. `fs set-default`, enable_multiple and the default file system are current: libcephfs mounted without client_fs or an fs name subscribes to the unqualified `mdsmap`, which the monitor serves from legacy_client_fscid.

features.name: Data pool list of a file system
features.summary: The `data_pools` list in the MDSMap that clients and the MDS use to validate file layouts and to report statfs.
features.description: `data_pools` starts with the data pool given to `fs new` (the default pool, which cannot be removed); `fs add_data_pool` runs the same pool checks as `fs new` and tags the pool with application `cephfs` (adding an existing pool succeeds), `fs rm_data_pool` refuses the first pool (EINVAL), silently succeeds for an absent pool and does not check whether layouts still use the pool. `sanitize` drops pools no longer in the OSDMap. The kernel validates layout ioctls against the list and reports the single pool in statfs when exactly one exists; libcephfs uses it for statfs; the C++ MDS validates layouts after waiting for the client's MDSMap epoch.

features.name: max_file_size published in the MDSMap
features.summary: The per-file-system maximum file size that clients enforce; the MDS only encodes and dumps it.
features.description: `max_file_size` defaults to 1 TiB and is set by `fs set <fs> max_file_size` (values below 65536 give ERANGE). The kernel sets `fsc->max_file_size = min(max_file_size, MAX_LFS_FILESIZE)` on every map; libcephfs checks it in `_do_setattr` (truncate) and `_write`. The C++ MDS performs no size check against it.

features.name: Mirroring metadata (MirrorInfo) in the FSMap
features.summary: Per-file-system mirroring state and peer list stored in the FSMap for cephfs-mirror; the MDS does not read it.
features.description: `fs mirror enable|disable <fs>`, `fs mirror peer_add <fs> <uuid> <client>@<cluster> <remote_fs>` and `peer_remove` edit `MirrorInfo{mirrored, peers}` where a peer is a uuid plus `{client_name, cluster_name, fs_name}`; peer operations need mirroring enabled and the spec must contain `@`; disable clears the peers. cephfs-mirror receives it through the `fsmap` subscription. `fs rename` and `fs swap` require mirroring disabled.
features.notes: See also F-CLU-001 (FSMap).

features.name: CompatSet encoding and the MDS incompat feature ids
features.summary: The three-mask feature set the monitor uses to decide which daemons may serve which file system.
features.description: A `CompatSet` is three `FeatureSet`s (compat, ro_compat, incompat), each a u64 mask plus `map<u64 id, string name>`; ids must be 1..63; bit 0 is set in memory and cleared on the wire; there is no version header. `A.readable(B)`: B.incompat is a subset of A.incompat; `A.writeable(B)`: readable and B.ro_compat a subset of A.ro_compat (plain `compat` ignored); `compare` returns 0 only if all masks are equal; `merge` copies missing features with their names. MDS incompat ids: 1 base v0.20, 2 client writeable ranges, 3 default file layouts on dirs, 4 dir inode in separate object, 5 versioned encoding, 6 dirfrag in omap, 7 inline data, 8 no anchor table, 9 file layout v2, 10 snaprealm v2, 11 minor log segments, 12 quiesce subvolumes. C++ daemons advertise all 12 (`get_compat_set_all`); new file systems get `default_compat` (all but 7 initially); no compat or ro_compat MDS features exist.
features.notes: Every mask bit needs a name: `merge` asserts on a missing name (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 7 item 1). Because `default_compat` is set once when the FSMap is created and only `mds compat rm_*` can change it, long-lived clusters keep the default of the release that created the FSMap.

features.name: Standby eligibility by compat set
features.summary: Compat filters that decide whether a standby may be promoted into (or follow a rank of) a file system.
features.description: A standby S is skipped for file system F when `!S.compat.writeable(F.compat)` (S lacks an incompat or ro_compat bit of F), or when F is not upgradeable and `!F.compat.writeable(S.compat)` (S has incompat/ro_compat bits F lacks). Plain compat bits never matter and only masks are compared, never names. A file system given a private incompat bit is never joined by daemons lacking it, and other file systems are unaffected (qa test_standby_incompat_reject, test_standby_incompat_reject_multifs).

features.name: Forced INLINE incompat bit and compat bootstrap
features.summary: The monitor inserts incompat 7 into every stored daemon and file system compat, which every daemon must then echo forever.
features.description: `FSMap::insert` (boot) replaces an empty boot compat by the v16.2.4 set and then always inserts incompat 7 ("mds uses inline data"); `MDSMap::decode` inserts 7 into the fs compat and into each `mds_info` compat (an empty one first inherits the fs compat), with a "TODO: remove after R is released" comment. `mds_info_t` before v10 decodes with the v16.2.4 set and MDSMap ev < 3 with the base set. Consequence: a daemon whose beacons omit bit 7 differs from its stored compat and is failed at its first beacon that reaches `prepare_beacon`.

legacy_parts.note: FSMap::insert replacing an empty boot compat with get_compat_set_v16_2_4(); mds_info_t::decode defaulting to the v16.2.4 set for struct_v < 10; MDSMap::decode defaulting to the base set for extended version < 3 and copying the fs compat into an empty mds_info compat. Commit d341c5b7734 (2022) added the INLINE insertion for upgrades from MDS daemons of v16.2.4 and older, but the current monitor applies it to every boot beacon and every decoded map, so a daemon at this commit whose beacons omit bit 7 is failed; the C++ MDS sends get_compat_set_all(), which contains bit 7. The empty-compat bootstrap and the decode defaults serve only boot beacons from MDS v16.2.4 and older and maps encoded by monitors that predate mds_info_t v10 (first in v16.2.6 and v17.1.0). The current MDS always sends a non-empty compat.

features.name: Compat set must not change after boot
features.summary: Every beacon must carry exactly the compat stored at boot, otherwise the monitor fails the daemon.
features.description: In `prepare_beacon`, if `beacon.compat.compare(info.compat) != 0` the monitor logs a clog WARN "compat changed unexpectedly" and calls `fail_mds_gid` (blocklisting a rank holder); the next beacon then gets a null map. The check is not in `preprocess_beacon`, so unchanged STANDBY beacons are acked without it; it fires on the first beacon that needs a proposal (a requested state change, changed health, a changed `mds_join_fs` resolution or clearing `laggy`), which can be long after boot.

features.name: Upgradeable file systems and compat merge on promotion
features.summary: The rule that lets a daemon with new incompat bits join a file system and permanently upgrades that file system's compat; cephadm upgrades depend on it.
features.description: `Filesystem::is_upgradeable()` is true when `in` is empty, or standby-replay is disallowed and either exactly one rank is in (even while it is up and healthy) or no rank is up. When `promote` moves a daemon whose compat the fs compat cannot write, it asserts upgradeability and merges the daemon compat into the fs compat permanently; afterwards daemons lacking those bits fail the eligibility filter for that file system. Standby-replay assignment never merges. cephadm's MDS upgrade disables `allow_standby_replay` and reduces `max_mds` to 1 (or runs `fs fail`) before restarting daemons, then waits for `up:active` in `fs dump`.
features.notes: Only `fs compat <fs> rm_*` (with no rank up) undoes a merge. `promote` hits `ceph_assert(fs.is_upgradeable())` if a standby-replay daemon left attached after `fs compat rm_incompat` is promoted while `allow_standby_replay` is set (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code). See also F-ADM-114 (cephadm upgrade choreography).

legacy_parts.note: Admitting and merging new incompat bits into a file system that already has ranks: is_upgradeable() through the standby-replay-disallowed clauses and the get_available_standby exception it controls, which exist for MDS upgrades across releases with different compat sets. At this commit `fs new` gives the new file system default_compat, which lacks INLINE (bit 7), and promotes standbys whose stored compat has bit 7 in the same pending map, so the promote-time merge already runs on `fs new` while `in` is empty (is_upgradeable() true). The other is_upgradeable() cases (standby-replay disallowed with exactly one rank in, or no rank up) matter only when a daemon carries incompat bits that an existing file system lacks, which happens when daemons of a release with additional bits replace older ones. cephadm and Rook run their MDS scale-down (allow_standby_replay off, max_mds 1 or fs fail) whenever they move MDS daemons to a new Ceph image or version.

features.name: fs compat and mds compat commands
features.summary: Operator commands that edit a file system's compat set or the default compat for new file systems.
features.description: `fs compat <fs> add_compat|add_incompat|rm_compat|rm_incompat <id> [<name>]` edits one fs compat only while no rank is up (EBUSY otherwise); id <= 0 is EINVAL, add needs a name (EINVAL), adding an existing id with a different name is EEXIST; there is no ro_compat sub-op. Deprecated `mds compat rm_compat|rm_incompat <id>` edits `default_compat`, used by later `fs new`/`fs reset`. `fs compat show` and `mds compat show` display them.
features.notes: `fs compat add_*` with id >= 64 reaches `ceph_assert(f.id < 64)` in `FeatureSet::insert` and aborts the monitor (inferred from code).

legacy_parts.note: The deprecated `mds compat show`, `mds compat rm_compat` and `mds compat rm_incompat` commands that operate on default_compat. `mds compat show`, `mds compat rm_compat` and `mds compat rm_incompat` are registered with FLAG(DEPRECATED) and are the only commands that show or edit default_compat; a grep of src/pybind/mgr, src/cephadm, src/tools and Rook's Go sources finds no use. `fs compat <fs> ...` and `fs compat show` are not deprecated.

features.name: mds_features in the boot beacon and get_up_features
features.summary: The messenger feature bits each daemon advertises at boot; MDS daemons AND them across all rank holders to choose encodings of stored and inter-rank data.
features.description: The beacon's u64 `mds_features` (the C++ MDS sends `CEPH_FEATURES_SUPPORTED_DEFAULT`) is stored in `mds_info_t::mds_features` at boot only and is not interpreted by the monitor. `MDSMap::get_up_features()` returns the AND over all rank holders; the C++ MDS uses it to pick encodings of journal events, inode stores, session maps and migration payloads.

legacy_parts.note: Selecting older encodings of journal events, inode stores, session maps, dirfrag commits and inter-rank payloads when the AND of the up ranks' mds_features lacks a bit (mixed-version ranks). Every C++ MDS at this commit reports CEPH_FEATURES_SUPPORTED_DEFAULT (= CEPH_FEATURES_ALL) as mds_features, so the AND over rank holders is the full set and the feature-dependent encoders take their current branches. The older branches reached through get_up_features() (file_layout_t without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2, entity_addr_t without MSG_ADDR2 or SERVER_NAUTILUS) are taken only when an older C++ MDS holds a rank of the same file system. The beacon field itself is still decoded, stored in mds_info_t and dumped by the current monitor.

features.name: MMDSBeacon message and the beacon sender thread
features.summary: The periodic MDS-to-monitor message that carries liveness, the wanted state, the last map epoch seen, compat, health and affinity.
features.description: `MSG_MDS_BEACON` = 100, HEAD_VERSION 8, COMPAT_VERSION 6, priority 196. Payload order: PaxosServiceMessage `version` (last MDSMap epoch seen), deprecated session mon (s16 -1) and tid (u64 0), fsid, `global_id` (MonClient global id), `state` (wanted state), `seq` (strictly increasing per process), `name`, `standby_for_rank`/`standby_for_name` (ignored), `compat`, `health` (`MDSHealth` v1 of `MDSHealthMetric` v1 {u16 type, u8 sev, message, metadata}), `sys_info` (only when state is `up:boot`), `mds_features`, `standby_for_fscid` (ignored), `standby_replay` (v>=7, ignored), `fs` (v>=8, `mds_join_fs`). A dedicated `mds-beacon` thread sends one whenever `0.9 * mds_beacon_interval` (4 s) has elapsed, using its own mutex and copies of epoch, wanted state, compat and health so it never needs `mds_lock`; the MonClient queues beacons while it has no mon session. `mds_beacon_interval` is read only at construction.
features.notes: `MDSHealthMetric` type 0 (`MDS_HEALTH_NULL`) hits `ceph_assert` in the monitor's decoder, so a beacon carrying it aborts the monitor that decodes it; decoding a v<7 beacon maps a requested `up:standby-replay` to `up:standby` (beacon-and-monitor section 3.4).

legacy_parts.note: MMDSBeacon::decode_payload handling of header versions 6 and 7: mapping a requested up:standby-replay to up:standby for v < 7 and omitting the fs (mds_join_fs) field for v < 8. The C++ MDS sends v8 beacons with the ignored standby fields filled with constants, and the current monitor decodes the whole v8 layout, so those vestigial fields are part of the current wire format. The decoder also accepts v6 beacons, last sent by 10.x MDS daemons, and v7 beacons, sent by 11.x to 14.x daemons; v8 first shipped in 15.2.0 (15.1.0 development tag).

features.name: Monitor beacon admission rules
features.summary: The checks the monitor applies to every beacon before it acts on it; a beacon failing them is ignored, acked only, or answered with a null map.
features.description: `PaxosService::dispatch` drops forwarded messages from older elections and disconnected sessions and **waits until the committed FSMap epoch is >= the beacon `version`**. `preprocess_beacon` then, in order: ignores sessions without mon cap `mds x`, a wrong fsid, or a source port 0; peons forward to the leader; an unknown gid not booting gets a null map; a duplicate boot is ignored; DNE goes to prepare; `state_seq > seq` is ignored ("old seq"); a `version` different from the daemon's effective epoch (its fs MDSMap epoch or `standby_epochs[gid]`) is **acked only, without processing the requested state or health**; laggy daemons, a changed `mds_join_fs` resolution, a changed state or changed health (type, severity, message) go to `prepare_beacon`; otherwise ack. The ack is an `MMDSBeacon` echoing the seq and state with empty health/compat; the MDS uses only the seq. Liveness (`last_beacon`) is noted for acked and prepared beacons but not for old-seq beacons or repeated `up:boot`.
features.notes: A beacon whose `version` is larger than the committed epoch stalls in `PaxosService::dispatch`; a stale epoch silently prevents state changes and health updates (beacon-and-monitor section 8). Clearing `laggy_since` also needs the new epoch, because marking a daemon laggy bumps its map epoch.

features.name: Beacon acks and MDS-side lagginess (self-fencing deferral)
features.summary: The MDS measures beacon acks and, when none arrived for `mds_beacon_grace`, stops processing all rank messages and periodic work until the monitor answers again.
features.description: Only `MSG_MDS_BEACON` from a monitor is accepted as an ack; it is matched by `seq`, `last_acked_stamp` becomes the send time of that beacon and laggy is cleared if the round trip is below `mds_beacon_grace`. `Beacon::is_laggy()` is true when `now - last_acked_stamp > mds_beacon_grace` (15 s, re-read at runtime) and is true until the first ack. While laggy: `MDSRankDispatcher::tick` returns before any upkeep (no session staleness, reconnect timeout, balancer, stopping passes, health refresh); every message reaching `MDSRank::_dispatch` (client and peer alike, except quiesce-DB peer messages) is appended to `waiting_for_nolaggy` and replayed in order by the progress thread afterwards; clients are not marked stale until `queue_max_age + session_timeout` after lagginess clears.
features.notes: Acks are dispatched on the same `ms_dispatch` thread that blocks on `mds_lock`, so a long `mds_lock` hold can make the daemon consider itself laggy although the monitor received its beacons. The progress thread is not woken when lagginess clears, so deferred messages wait for the next tick or message (process-and-threading section 8).

features.name: Heartbeat-gated beacons (internal watchdog)
features.summary: A daemon that is alive but wedged stops sending beacons so the monitor fails it over.
features.description: `Beacon::_send` skips the beacon (retrying every 0.5 s) while `HeartbeatMap::is_healthy()` is false. The only heartbeat worker is the "MDSRank" handle, re-armed by `heartbeat_reset()` to now + `mds_heartbeat_grace` (15 s) with **no suicide grace** ("the mon takes care of killing us"); it is reset at tick start, after each dispatched message, on every `MDSContext::complete` and every `mds_heartbeat_reset_grace` (1000) iterations of long loops. A rankless standby has no worker and is always healthy. The `lockup <ms>` admin command and `heartbeat_inject_failure` test this path.
features.notes: `mds_heartbeat_reset_grace` is documented in seconds but used as an iteration count. Large-cache rejoin handlers without heartbeat resets (`recalc_auth_bits`, `trim_non_auth`, `rejoin_send_acks`, ...) can exceed the grace and cause a failover that restarts recovery (resolve-and-rejoin section 3.20).

features.name: Boot registration as a standby with daemon metadata
features.summary: An `up:boot` beacon from an unknown gid registers the daemon in the shared standby pool and stores its system metadata.
features.description: `prepare_beacon` inserts `mds_info_t{gid, name, addrs = message source addrs, mds_features, state = up:standby, state_seq = seq, compat, join_fscid}` with `FSMap::insert`, initialises `last_beacon[gid]` and stores `sys_info` as daemon metadata under `mds_metadata/last_metadata` (keys from `collect_sys_info`: ceph_version, ceph_version_short, ceph_release, os, kernel_*, hostname, arch, mem_*, cpu, distro*, container keys, plus `addr`). The daemon keeps `want_state = up:boot` until a map lists it as `up:standby` ("Monitors have assigned me to become a standby"); a daemon that keeps sending `up:boot` after its standby epoch is ignored without liveness and is eventually removed as laggy. The MgrClient is started and `mgrmap` subscribed the first time the daemon appears in a map.
features.notes: mgr re-reads `mds metadata` when the metadata `addr` differs from `stringify(info.addrs)` (`src/mgr/Mgr.cc:753-822`); `mds metadata`, `ceph versions` and `mds count-metadata` read the stored `sys_info`.

features.name: Unique daemon names
features.summary: A booting daemon replaces (fails) any existing daemon with the same name.
features.description: With `mds_enforce_unique_name` (default true) a boot beacon makes the monitor `fail_mds_gid` every existing daemon with the same name ("<name> restarted"), blocklisting it if it held a rank; this needs a writeable OSDMap (retried otherwise). `ceph-mds` refuses an id that is empty or starts with a digit, because `gid_from_arg` reads a numeric argument as a rank or gid, never as a name.
features.notes: Two hosts sharing an MDS id flap each other; a respawned process (new gid, same name) fails its own previous gid through this rule (beacon-and-monitor sections 3.11 and 8).

features.name: DNE beacon on clean shutdown
features.summary: On orderly exit the MDS tells the monitor it is going away, so its rank fails over immediately instead of after the beacon grace.
features.description: On SIGINT/SIGTERM or asok `exit`, `MDSDaemon::suicide` sets `want_state = down:dne`, releases `mds_lock` and, if the gid is still in its map, sends a beacon and waits up to 0.95 s for its ack (`send_and_wait(1)`). The monitor acks immediately (so the wait returns) and then evicts the daemon with `fail_mds_gid`, which blocklists a rank holder for `mon_mds_blocklist_interval`; the replacement is promoted at the next monitor tick.
features.notes: A clean shutdown of an active still blocklists its addresses for a day; harmless because every new process has a new nonce, but the blocklist grows with restarts (beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.name: Health metrics carried in beacons
features.summary: Beacon side of the health metric pipeline.
features.description: See F-ADM-073 for the metric encoding and how the monitor turns metrics into checks. Beacon-side facts: Beacon::notify_health recomputes the list at the end of every non-laggy rank tick (and in damaged()) and every MMDSBeacon carries the latest snapshot; standbys report none. The monitor stores the latest health per gid (pending_daemon_health, persisted as mds_health/<gid>) and uses it to gate commands (F-ADM-083).
features.notes: Health equality includes the message text, so a changing text sends every beacon through `prepare_beacon` and bumps the MDSMap epoch (map churn to all clients). A new leader does not reload `pending_daemon_health`, so the command health gates see no metrics until each daemon beacons again (beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.name: Monitor-side laggy detection and its protections
features.summary: The leader marks a daemon laggy when no beacon was noted for `mds_beacon_grace`, with guards against monitor-side outages.
features.description: Every tick (`mon_tick_interval` 5 s) the leader checks `last_beacon`: a daemon silent for `mds_beacon_grace` (15 s, the monitor's own config) gets `laggy_since = now` (a proposal, so clients see the rank laggy), and if the OSDMap is writeable and some MDS beaconed within `max(mds_beacon_interval, mds_beacon_grace/2)` it is queued for removal or replacement. Protections: while a monitor is down or the quorum is younger than `mds_beacon_mon_down_grace` (60 s), nothing is done until the silence exceeds that grace; if the tick itself was delayed by more than `grace - interval` (11 s) all beacon stamps are reset to now; a new leader starts with every daemon stamped now. Frozen daemons are never dropped. Laggy is cleared in `prepare_beacon` by the next beacon carrying the current epoch.
features.notes: `mds_beacon_grace` and `mds_beacon_interval` are declared `services: mds` but the monitor uses its own values; inconsistent settings make monitor and MDS disagree on lagginess. A laggy holder without a replacement stays in `up` with `laggy_since` indefinitely; ceph-fuse then refuses new mounts (beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.name: Standby selection scoring
features.summary: How the monitor picks a standby from the shared pool for a rank of a file system.
features.description: `get_available_standby(fs, avoid_addrs)` scans `standby_daemons` in ascending gid order, skips laggy, frozen and compat-ineligible daemons and scores the rest: join_fscid equal to the fs 6 (3 on the same host), NONE 5 (2), another fs 4 (1, skipped entirely if the fs has REFUSE_STANDBY_FOR_ANOTHER_FS); the highest score wins, ties go to the lowest gid, and the scan stops at a 6. `find_replacement_for(rank)` first returns the rank's standby-replay follower (or nothing at all if that follower is frozen), otherwise calls `get_available_standby` with the current holder's addresses as `avoid_addrs` when the rank is still up.
features.notes: A lower-scored eligible standby is used when no better one exists; ranking is not prevention (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 3.9).

features.name: mds_join_fs file system affinity
features.summary: Each daemon names a preferred file system in its beacons; the monitor uses it for standby scoring and affinity swaps.
features.description: The beacon `fs` field carries `mds_join_fs` (read on every send, so runtime changes apply at once); the monitor resolves the **name** to an fscid at boot and on every later beacon that reaches `prepare_beacon`, storing NONE if no fs has that name, and a changed resolution forces a proposal. Removing a file system resets every `join_fscid` that pointed to it. cephadm sets `mds_join_fs = <service_id>` for every MDS service it deploys.
features.notes: Affinity follows the name: after `fs rename` it silently drops to NONE, and after `fs swap --swap-fscids=no` it follows the name to the other fscid (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code). See also F-ADM-113 (cephadm deployment).

features.name: Per-file-system selection flags: refuse_standby_for_another_fs and host anti-affinity
features.summary: Two file system settings that restrict or bias which standbys the monitor selects.
features.description: `fs set <fs> refuse_standby_for_another_fs true` (flag 1<<7) excludes standbys whose `join_fscid` names another file system; vanilla (NONE) standbys remain eligible. `standby_enable_host_anti_affinity` (default true, ev >= 20) makes any different-host candidate beat every same-host candidate, including an exact affinity match, when an `avoid_addrs` set is supplied: replacing an up (laggy) holder, choosing a standby-replay follower, or an affinity swap; failed and new ranks get no anti-affinity. Host equality compares only the IP of the standby's first address with every address of the holder.

features.name: Affinity-driven swaps of healthy daemons
features.summary: The monitor replaces a healthy active or standby-replay daemon whose affinity is worse than an available standby's.
features.description: Per joinable and resizeable file system with a writeable OSDMap, at most once per tick, for each daemon whose `join_fscid` is not the fs: compute a candidate (standby-replay: `get_available_standby` avoiding the followed host; active: `find_replacement_for`); stop scanning at the first daemon without a candidate; if the candidate has strictly better affinity (exact match, or vanilla when the daemon prefers another fs), a standby-replay is failed (re-assigned later) and an active is failed over with `drop_mds` (blocklist plus promotion).
features.notes: Any daemon state other than ACTIVE or STANDBY_REPLAY in a resizeable file system aborts the monitor here (`ceph_abort_msg("invalid state in MDSMap")`); valid beacons cannot produce such a state, only `mds set_state` can (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code).

features.name: Failed-rank and laggy-holder replacement
features.summary: Ranks without a live holder get a standby promoted into `up:replay`; a laggy holder is replaced only when a replacement exists.
features.description: `maybe_promote_standby` (every tick, unless NOT_JOINABLE) gives each rank in `failed` the result of `find_replacement_for` and promotes it to `up:replay` (clog "Standby ... assigned to filesystem ... as rank"). For a laggy daemon, `drop_mds` removes standbys and standby-replay followers without blocklisting; a laggy rank holder is failed (blocklisted) and its replacement promoted in the same tick **only if** a replacement exists and the file system is joinable; otherwise it stays in `up` with `laggy_since` until it beacons again or a standby appears. Typical detection-to-promotion time with defaults is 15-20 s plus the Paxos commit.

features.name: Promotion into a rank and the initial rank state
features.summary: The monitor, never the MDS, decides which rank a daemon holds and whether it starts by creating, starting or replaying it.
features.description: `FSMap::promote(gid, fscid, rank)` moves a standby (or the rank's standby-replay follower, in place) into the file system: state `up:starting` if the rank was in `stopped` (removed from it), `up:creating` if the rank is not `is_in` (never existed or forgotten), else `up:replay` (removed from `failed`); sets `rank` and `inc` = pending FSMap epoch, adds the rank to `in` and `up`, may merge compat, and bumps the MDSMap epoch. Callers: `maybe_resize_cluster` (growth), `maybe_promote_standby` (failed ranks), `drop_mds` (laggy holders, affinity swaps) and `fs new` (ranks 0..max_mds-1 in `up:creating`). The MDS must implement every entry state the monitor can assign and cannot refuse an assignment.

features.name: Fencing failed rank holders with OSD blocklists
features.summary: When the monitor removes a rank holder it blocklists every address of that daemon at the OSDs in the same Paxos transaction.
features.description: `fail_mds_gid` (used by laggy replacement, beacon evictions, DNE, unique-name enforcement, affinity swaps, `mds fail`, `fs fail`) blocklists, only if the daemon holds a rank and is not standby-replay, every address of its address vector with `TYPE_ANY` until now + `mon_mds_blocklist_interval` (1 day), forces an immediate proposal, then `FSMap::erase(gid, blocklist_epoch)`. FSMap and OSDMap changes made under `paxos.plug()` commit together. Entries are exact `ip:port/nonce` instances, so a restarted process with a new nonce is unaffected. The fenced daemon sees `-EBLOCKLISTED` on writes. Standbys, standby-replay followers and daemons that report `down:stopped` are not blocklisted; `mds rm` bypasses blocklisting.
features.notes: See also F-PROTO-106 (fencing identity).

features.name: Wait for last_failure_osd_epoch before touching rank objects
features.summary: A daemon taking over a failed rank waits until its OSDMap includes the blocklist of the previous holder before reading the journal.
features.description: `FSMap::erase` records the caller's blocklist epoch in the MDSMap `last_failure_osd_epoch`. `replay_start` (for `up:replay` and `up:standby-replay`) waits until the Objecter has an OSDMap with epoch >= that value before `boot_start`; a promoted standby-replay follower waits again before its final takeover pass. `up:creating` and `up:starting` do not wait.
features.notes: `last_failure_osd_epoch` can go backwards to 0: `FSMap::erase` overwrites it for every erased daemon of the fs, with 0 when nothing was blocklisted (standby-replay removal, `FSMap::stop`, `mds rm`). Concrete paths by code reading: one `check_health` tick dropping a laggy holder then a laggy follower of another rank with a higher gid, and `fs fail` (daemons failed in gid order). The replacement then does not wait for the blocklist epoch; impact not tested (beacon-and-monitor section 8, rank-lifecycle gotcha 20). See also F-STORE-042 (OSD-side guarantee), F-CLU-036.

features.name: Rank incarnation
features.summary: The FSMap epoch at which the current holder was promoted; distinguishes successive holders of the same rank.
features.description: `promote` sets `mds_info_t::inc` to the pending FSMap epoch; `assign_standby_replay` does not, so a follower carries `inc = 0` until promoted. The C++ MDS passes it to the Objecter as the OSD client incarnation, so OSD request ids `(mds.<rank>, incarnation, tid)` of two holders of the same rank never collide in OSD duplicate detection. libcephfs treats an incarnation change of a rank as a restart (old state counted as NULL); peers in `up:resolve` or later use an incarnation change to detect a restarted rank.
features.notes: See also F-STORE-091 (RADOS identity).

features.name: Standby-replay assignment
features.summary: With `allow_standby_replay`, the monitor attaches standbys as hot followers of active ranks; a follower is the preferred replacement for its rank.
features.description: When the file system is joinable and resizeable and has ALLOW_STANDBY_REPLAY (1<<5), `maybe_promote_standby` repeatedly assigns an available standby (anti-affinity against the followed holder) to each followable rank (up, holder not in replay..clientreplay, no follower yet) via `assign_standby_replay` (state `up:standby-replay`, rank = followed rank, not in `up`, no compat merge). `fs set <fs> allow_standby_replay false` fails every follower (no blocklist). A follower may report only its own state or `down:damaged`; any other requested state evicts it. The kernel client ignores follower entries (state <= 0).
features.notes: A frozen follower blocks replacement of its rank completely. A DAMAGED report from a follower blocklists the healthy active and marks the rank damaged; if the followed rank is not up at that moment, `MDSMap::get_gid` throws inside a `noexcept` function and terminates the leader monitor (beacon-and-monitor section 8, inferred from code).

features.name: Growing the number of active ranks (max_mds)
features.summary: The monitor adds ranks one at a time towards `max_mds`, each new rank starting in `up:creating` or `up:starting`.
features.description: `fs set <fs> max_mds N` (1..256) sets `max_mds` and clears NOT_JOINABLE; it requires `--yes-i-really-mean-it` when any MDS in the cluster reports any health metric, and is EINVAL above 1 when snapshots were ever allowed without `allow_multimds_snaps`. Each tick, if both the committed and pending maps are resizeable and the fs is joinable with `size(in) < max_mds`, the lowest rank not `is_in` gets `find_replacement_for` + `promote` (`up:creating` or `up:starting`); because those states make the map non-resizeable, ranks are added strictly one after another.

features.name: Shrinking: monitor-driven up:stopping and FSMap::stop
features.summary: When `in > max_mds` the monitor asks the highest rank to stop and, once it reports `down:stopped`, removes the rank.
features.description: Each tick, if both maps are resizeable and `size(in) > max_mds`, rank `size(in)-1` is set to `up:stopping` if it is `up:active` (otherwise nothing that tick); `up:stopping` keeps the map non-resizeable, so ranks stop one at a time. On a `down:stopped` beacon the monitor logs "finished stopping rank", `FSMap::stop` removes the rank from `up` and `in`, adds it to `stopped`, erases the daemon and every standby-replay follower of that rank, and replies with a null MDSMap so the daemon respawns as a new standby.

features.name: fs new
features.summary: Creates a file system from existing pools and immediately assigns standbys to its ranks.
features.description: `fs new <fs> <meta> <data> [--force] [--allow-dangerous-metadata-overlay] [--fscid N] [--recover] [--set k v ...]` (fs rw) checks: pools exist (ENOENT), data pool id 0 refused, same name with same pools succeeds as a no-op (else EINVAL), metadata pool empty unless `--force`, a second fs needs `enable_multiple`, pools used by another fs need the overlay flag, `--fscid` needs `--force` and a free id, and `_check_pool` (no mon-managed snaps, EC metadata refused, EC default data needs `--force`, EC data needs overwrites, no cache tier, no other application). It creates the `Filesystem` (compat = `default_compat`, max_mds 1), applies `--set` values, tags both pools with application `cephfs`, sets metadata pool `recovery_priority 5`, `pg_num_min 16`, `pg_autoscale_bias 4`, and promotes standbys to `up:creating` for ranks 0..max_mds-1 in the same pending map. With `--recover`, rank 0 is put in `in` and `failed` with NOT_JOINABLE and nothing is assigned, so the first holder replays existing metadata.
features.notes: `fs new` ignores `joinable false` given via `--set`; only `--set down true` or `--recover` create a file system without immediate assignment (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code). See also F-STORE-101 (pool requirements).

features.name: fs rm
features.summary: Deletes an offline file system from the FSMap; RADOS pools are untouched.
features.description: `fs rm <fs> --yes-i-really-mean-it` (fs rw) requires that no rank is up (EINVAL) and the confirmation (EPERM); a missing fs succeeds. It clears `legacy_client_fscid` if it named this fs (no new default is chosen), fails remaining standby-replay daemons, erases the `Filesystem` and resets `join_fscid` of daemons pointing at it; subscribers of `mdsmap.<fscid>` receive nothing more.

features.name: fs fail and the joinable flag
features.summary: Takes a whole file system offline (all daemons removed, no new assignments) and brings it back.
features.description: `fs fail <fs> [--yes-i-really-mean-it]` sets NOT_JOINABLE and `fail_mds_gid`s every daemon of the fs in ascending gid order: holders are blocklisted, ranks go to `failed` (a CREATING rank is forgotten, a STARTING rank returns to `stopped`), followers are removed; it is EPERM without confirmation when a daemon reports TRIM or CACHE_OVERSIZED. `fs set <fs> joinable false|true` (deprecated inverse alias `cluster_down`) sets/clears NOT_JOINABLE: while set there is no failed-rank promotion, no standby-replay assignment, no growth (shrink still proceeds), no laggy-holder replacement and no affinity swap; laggy standbys and followers are still removed. `fs set max_mds` also clears the flag.
features.notes: Because `fs fail` erases daemons in gid order, a standby-replay follower with a higher gid than a holder resets `last_failure_osd_epoch` to 0 after the holder was blocklisted (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8).

legacy_parts.note: The deprecated `fs set <fs> cluster_down` alias of `joinable`. `fs set <fs> cluster_down` is handled in the joinable branch with the value inverted, and the monitor appends 'WARNING: cluster_down flag is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Please use "joinable".' to its output. A grep of src/pybind/mgr, src/cephadm, src/tools and Rook's Go sources finds no use; `fs fail` and `joinable` are current (cephadm's MDS upgrade issues `fs fail`).

features.name: fs reset
features.summary: Disaster-recovery command that replaces a file system's MDSMap by a fresh one whose rank 0 must replay.
features.description: `fs reset <fs> --yes-i-really-mean-it` requires an existing fs (ENOENT), no rank up (EINVAL) and the confirmation (EPERM). `reset_filesystem` keeps only fscid, name, pools, `cas_pool`, `inline_data_enabled` and `standby_count_wanted`; compat becomes `default_compat`, `in = {0}`, `failed = {0}`, every other previously used rank goes to `stopped`, and flags (including NOT_JOINABLE), `max_mds` (1), timeouts, sizes, required features, balancer and mirror info return to defaults. On the next tick rank 0 is replaced and its holder enters `up:replay`.
features.notes: The reset MDSMap keeps epoch 0 until modified again; standby-replay daemons are not failed, which leaves an `mds_roles` entry without `mds_info` that `sanity()` rejects (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 8, inferred from code).

features.name: fs set down
features.summary: Stops every rank of a file system cleanly and later restores the previous rank count.
features.description: `fs set <fs> down true` saves `old_max_mds = max_mds` and sets `max_mds = 0` without touching flags, so the monitor stops ranks one by one (`up:stopping` to `down:stopped`) until `in` is empty; `down false` restores `max_mds = old_max_mds` (or 1) and ranks regrow as `up:starting`; `down false` while `max_mds > 0` is a no-op ("already online").
features.notes: The last rank to stop evicts and (by default) blocklists every mounted client, so clients must remount after `down false` (rank-lifecycle gotcha 25).

features.name: fs rename and fs swap
features.summary: Renames an offline file system, or swaps the names (and optionally fscids) of two offline file systems.
features.description: `fs rename <fs> <new> --yes-i-really-mean-it` requires a free target name (EINVAL), mirroring disabled (EPERM), the confirmation and the fs offline with `refuse_client_session` set (EPERM); it rewrites the pool application tags and `fs_name`. `fs swap <fs1> <id1> <fs2> <id2> --swap-fscids=yes|no --yes-i-really-mean-it` requires both to exist with matching ids, mirroring disabled, both offline and both `refuse_client_session`; `swap_fscids` exchanges the two `Filesystem` objects without updating `mds_roles`, `join_fscid` or `legacy_client_fscid`.
features.notes: Kernel clients mounted with the old `mds_namespace` fail the next map decode and are unmounted, which is why the fs must be offline with `refuse_client_session`.

features.name: mds fail
features.summary: Fails one daemon by role, gid or name; a rank holder is blocklisted and replaced at the next tick.
features.description: `mds fail <role|gid|name> [--yes-i-really-mean-it]` (mds rw) resolves the argument as a role if that rank is up, else as an integer gid, else as a daemon name, and calls `fail_mds_gid`: a rank holder (not standby-replay) is blocklisted, its rank goes to `failed` and is replaced next tick (its follower first); a standby or follower is just removed and respawns as a new standby. It returns 0 with a message when the target is unknown, and EPERM without confirmation when the target reports TRIM or CACHE_OVERSIZED.

features.name: Damaged ranks and mds repaired
features.summary: A rank reported damaged is quarantined (never reassigned) until an operator runs `mds repaired`.
features.description: On a `down:damaged` beacon from the holder or its standby-replay follower the monitor (with a writeable OSDMap) blocklists the **holder's** addresses, fails the follower, runs `FSMap::damaged` (erase, then move the rank from `failed` to `damaged`; it stays in `in`) and proposes immediately. A damaged rank blocks `is_resolving`/`is_rejoining`, keeps the map degraded and raises `MDS_DAMAGE` (HEALTH_ERR). `mds repaired <role>` (`FSMap::undamaged`) moves it back to `failed`, so it is replaced at the next tick.
features.notes: A DAMAGED report from a CREATING holder leaves the rank in `damaged` but not in `in` (inferred from code). A follower reporting DAMAGED while its rank is not up terminates the leader monitor via `up.at()` in a `noexcept` function (beacon-and-monitor section 8, not tested).

features.name: Hidden and debug rank commands: mds rm, rmfailed, freeze, set_state
features.summary: Low-level monitor commands that edit daemon and rank records without the normal checks.
features.description: `mds rm <gid>` erases a daemon in a state <= 0 (EBUSY otherwise; unknown gid succeeds) without blocklisting, which includes CREATING and STARTING holders. `mds rmfailed <role> --yes-i-really-mean-it` removes a rank from `failed` only: it stays in `in`, is never replaced and is handed out as CREATING only by growth. `mds freeze <role|gid> <bool>` sets `mds_info_t::flags` FROZEN: frozen daemons are never selected or dropped, and a frozen follower blocks replacement of its rank. `mds set_state <gid> <n>` writes the state without validation.
features.notes: `mds set_state` on a standby gid trips `ceph_assert(info.state == STATE_STANDBY)` in `FSMap::modify_daemon` and aborts the leader; a shrink whose target is a `rmfailed` rank terminates the monitor via `up.at()` (code reading, not tested). `mds rm` leaves the gid's health entry behind, still counted by `has_any_health_warning`.

features.name: Read-only fs and mds commands and the fs dump layout
features.summary: Inspection commands whose JSON output orchestrators, mgr modules and tools parse.
features.description: Commands: `fs dump [epoch]` (any stored epoch, unfiltered when historical), `fs get <fs>`, `fs ls`, `fs lsflags <fs>`, `fs feature ls`, `fs compat show <fs>`, `mds compat show`, `mds stat`, `mds metadata [who]`, `mds versions`, `mds count-metadata <field>`, `mds last-seen <name>`; `fs ls/get/lsflags` need `fs r`, the rest `mds r`. `fs dump` JSON: top-level `epoch, btime, default_fscid, compat, feature_flags, standbys[], filesystems[]{mdsmap, id, mirror_info}`; `mdsmap` keys include `flags_state`, `in`, `up{mds_<rank>: gid}`, `failed`, `damaged`, `stopped`, `info{gid_<gid>: {gid, name, rank, incarnation, state, state_seq, addr, addrs, join_fscid, laggy_since, export_targets, features, flags, compat}}` with state strings such as `up:active` that cephadm waits on. `mds last-seen` uses an in-memory history pruned after `mon_fsmap_prune_threshold` (300 s).

legacy_parts.note: The deprecated `mds compat show` command. `mds compat show` is registered with FLAG(DEPRECATED) and no mgr module, cephadm, Rook or tool issues it (grep). The other listed commands and the fs dump layout are current: cephadm waits on the up:active state string and mgr/prometheus reads the per-daemon addr field.

features.name: Orchestration helpers: mds ok-to-stop, last-seen, metadata, versions
features.summary: Commands orchestrators use to decide whether MDS daemons can be stopped or upgraded.
features.description: `mds ok-to-stop <ids...>` returns EBUSY if any file system is degraded, or if the standbys left after stopping the listed ones are fewer than the listed rank holders that have no standby-replay follower outside the list; unknown ids are skipped. `mds last-seen <name>` gives seconds since the daemon was last in an FSMap (0 if in the latest). `mds metadata`, `mds versions` and `mds count-metadata` read the boot `sys_info`.
features.notes: See also F-ADM-116 (Rook ok-to-stop gate).

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: Daemon and rank states: numeric values and names
features.summary: The wire values of every daemon and rank state and the strings tools display for them.
features.description: Values (`ceph_fs.h`): dne 0, stopped -1, boot -4, standby -5, creating -6, starting -7, standby-replay -8, replayonce -9 (unused), null -10, replay 8, resolve 9, reconnect 10, rejoin 11, clientreplay 12, active 13, stopping 14, damaged 15; names `up:active`, `down:stopped`, ... from `ceph_mds_state_name`. Values > 0 mean the rank is in. BOOT, DNE, STOPPED and DAMAGED are beacon values never stored as a daemon state; failed/stopped/damaged/dne are rank conditions expressed by set membership. CREATING/STARTING/REPLAY/STANDBY_REPLAY/STOPPING are imposed by the monitor; RESOLVE through ACTIVE, STOPPED, DAMAGED and DNE are requested by the MDS. `mds_info_t::is_degraded()` is REPLAY <= state <= CLIENTREPLAY.
features.notes: `doc/cephfs/mds-states.rst` spells `up:standby_replay`; the code string is `up:standby-replay` (rank-lifecycle gotcha 30).

legacy_parts.note: State value -9 (replayonce, 'up:oneshot-replay'). CEPH_MDS_STATE_REPLAYONCE (-9) is commented 'Legacy, unused', is not a member of MDSMap::DaemonState, and no MDS, monitor or kernel code assigns it; only the name tables map it to 'up:oneshot-replay'.

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: State transition validation on both sides
features.summary: The legal state graph, enforced by the monitor on requested states and by the C++ MDS on assigned states.
features.description: `MDSMap::state_transition_valid(prev, next)`: same state and DAMAGED always valid; BOOT to STANDBY; STANDBY to STANDBY_REPLAY, REPLAY, CREATING, STARTING; CREATING/STARTING to ACTIVE; STANDBY_REPLAY to REPLAY; REPLAY to RESOLVE or RECONNECT; RESOLVE, RECONNECT, CLIENTREPLAY to prev+1; REJOIN to CLIENTREPLAY, ACTIVE or STOPPED; ACTIVE to STOPPING; STOPPING to STOPPED; anything else invalid. The monitor evicts (with blocklisting for rank holders) a holder that reports an invalid transition, a standby that requests any other state, and a follower that requests anything but its state or DAMAGED. The C++ MDS respawns when a received map shows an invalid transition for itself. Removal is not a transition. The monitor does not check cluster-wide preconditions and has no per-state timeout.

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: Requesting the next state through beacons
features.summary: The MDS moves a rank forward only by asking the monitor and acting when the new map shows the state.
features.description: `request_state(s)` calls `Beacon::set_want_state(mdsmap, s)`, which updates the wanted state and the last-seen epoch under one lock so a beacon never carries a new epoch with a stale state, and sends a beacon at once; periodic beacons repeat it. The monitor applies it only when the beacon epoch equals the daemon's current effective epoch, records `state` and `state_seq`, logs "is now active" on the first `up:active`, and pushes the new map. The MDS acts in `handle_mds_map`, not at request time. Each MDS-driven step therefore costs a beacon round trip and a Paxos commit; a single-rank failover from replay to active needs 3 or 4 committed epochs. To close races the MDS compares against `get_want_state()`: replayed requests, dirty cap flushes and reconnect messages that arrive before it sees its own `up:reconnect` map are admitted or parked.
features.notes: A beacon carrying the latest epoch with the pre-assignment state is an invalid transition and evicts the daemon with a blocklist, which is why epoch and state are updated atomically (beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: Rank sets and derived predicates
features.summary: The sets `in/up/failed/stopped/damaged` and the predicates computed from them that gate resizing, standby-replay, recovery barriers and client availability.
features.description: Effective rule: `up` keys + `failed` + `damaged` = `in` (the header comment `up + failed = in` predates `damaged`); `is_in(r)` is up or failed (not damaged). Predicates: `is_degraded()` = failed or damaged non-empty or any daemon in REPLAY..CLIENTREPLAY; `is_resizeable()` = not degraded and no CREATING/STARTING/STOPPING; `is_followable(r)`; `is_resolving()` = some RESOLVE, no REPLAY, no failed/damaged; `is_rejoining()` = some REJOIN, none in REPLAY/RESOLVE/RECONNECT, no failed/damaged; `get_recovery_mds_set` = failed + damaged + ranks in REPLAY..STOPPING; `get_mds_set_lower_bound`; `get_down_mds_set` = failed + damaged; `is_cluster_available()`. Implicit rank state without holder: failed, stopped (`down:stopped`), damaged (`down:damaged`), else dne.
features.notes: Edge cases break the set rule: a DAMAGED report from a CREATING holder leaves the rank damaged but not in `in`; `mds rmfailed` leaves a rank in `in` only (fsmap-and-mdsmap section 3.4).

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: Daemon-level map handling
features.summary: How the daemon reacts to each new MDSMap before any rank logic: compat check, removal, standby, rank assignment.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::handle_mds_map` (under `mds_lock`; maps accepted from monitors and peer MDSs): drop epochs <= current; decode; `sub_got`; **suicide if `get_compat_set_all()` cannot write the map compat**; compute the rank (for a follower, the followed rank); present in the old map and absent from the new one: respawn ("Map removed me"); first appearance: start the MgrClient and subscribe `mgrmap`; mark down connections to gids that left; rankless: NULL to STANDBY sets `want_state = up:standby`, NULL stays booting, any other rankless state aborts; with a rank: respawn if it differs from the existing rank object, else create `MDSRankDispatcher` once and call its map handler; finally record the epoch for later beacons. A rank object is never replaced in-process: a rank change, removal or invalid transition re-execs the process.

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: Rank-level map handling and peer change detection
features.summary: The single per-rank driver that starts each phase and detects peer ranks failing, restarting, recovering or stopping.
features.description: `MDSRankDispatcher::handle_mds_map`: treats an old NULL state as STANDBY, asserts no map was missed, validates the transition (respawn if invalid), renames the messenger and pushes the incarnation on a state change; evicts sessions lacking `required_client_features` (state >= RECONNECT); caches `is_degraded`. From `up:resolve` on it detects peers newly down (`handle_mds_failure`), restarted (incarnation change while REPLAY/RESOLVE) or stopped-and-restarted. It then calls exactly one of `replay_start`, `resolve_start`, `reconnect_start`, `rejoin_start`, `clientreplay_start`, `active_start` (after `recovery_done`), `boot_create`, `boot_start`, `stopping_start`; runs snap-table recovery, the resolve and rejoin triggers, kicks waiters for cluster recovery, bootstrapping peers, recovered peers and `waiting_for_mdsmap`; while active raises the OSD epoch barrier and sets the journal fadvise hint (none if a follower exists, else DONTNEED).

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: MDSMap epoch waits for client requests
features.summary: Requests that name a pool or create a snapshot wait until the MDS has at least the client's MDSMap epoch.
features.description: Every client request carries the client's MDSMap epoch (`mdsmap_epoch` in the request head). Before validating a pool in a layout (open with O_CREAT and a layout, setlayout, setdirlayout) or the ALLOW_SNAPS flag for mksnap, the C++ MDS parks the request with `wait_for_mdsmap(epoch)` until its own map is at least that new; `handle_mds_map` wakes waiters for epochs <= the new one. The migrator uses the same queue. Replies carry the MDS's epoch.

features.group: Rank state machine and map handling
features.name: File-system health checks derived from the map
features.summary: Map-side inputs of the file-system health checks the monitor derives from the FSMap.
features.description: See F-ADM-082 for the checks. Map-side inputs: the checks are computed from rank states, the failed and damaged sets, max_mds and the standby pool. `standby_count_wanted` defaults to -1 and is auto-set to 1 by the monitor tick once an active rank and a standby or follower exist; `fs set <fs> standby_count_wanted <n>` (>= 0) changes it. `ceph status` summarises daemons and file systems from the FSMap.
features.notes: The per-rank detail of `FS_DEGRADED` ("is replaying journal", ...) is built into a local list and dropped; the daemon metric `MDS_HEALTH_DAMAGE` and the damaged-rank check share the code `MDS_DAMAGE`; one shared standby satisfies `standby_count_wanted = 1` on every file system (fsmap-and-mdsmap and beacon-and-monitor section 8).

features.name: Boot stages for up:starting, up:replay and up:standby-replay
features.summary: The ordered loading of per-rank objects before a rank can replay or serve, and the error mapping of each step.
features.description: `boot_start` is a four-step continuation chain. INITIAL: default layouts; in one gather `InoTable::load` (`mds<r>_inotable`), `SessionMap::load` (omap of `mds<r>_sessionmap`, 1024 keys per read; every loaded session becomes open), `MDLog::open` (JournalPointer `<0x400+r>.00000000`, journal header, end probe), `PurgeQueue::open` (`<0x500+r>`), rank 0 also `SnapServer::load` (`mds_snaptable`); for replay the purge queue and `OpenFileTable::load` start outside the gather; standby-replay opens neither. OPEN_ROOT: mdsdir inode `<0x100+r>.00000000.inode` (and its dirfrag for starting), the global snaprealm, rank 0 the root inode. PREPARE_LOG: starting appends an `ESubtreeMap`; replay waits for purge-queue recovery and journal replay. REPLAY_DONE: `validate_sessions` then `replay_done`. Errors: `-EAGAIN` in standby-replay respawns; `-EINVAL`/`-ENOENT` mark the rank damaged; `-EROFS` continues read-only; others suicide. IO completions respawn on `-EBLOCKLISTED`/`-ETIMEDOUT` first. `validate_sessions` marks the rank damaged if a session's preallocated inode range intersects the InoTable free set (tracker 16842).
features.notes: Object formats belong to [mds-tables](../cpp-map/07-storage-formats/mds-tables.md) and [rados-object-catalog](../cpp-map/07-storage-formats/rados-object-catalog.md). A purge-queue open failure after `wait_for_recovery` is registered delivers the raw error (fatal), before it yields `-EROFS` (tolerated) (rank-lifecycle gotcha 28). See also F-STORE-056 (storage view), F-STORE-037 (replay pipeline).

features.name: Creating a new rank (up:creating)
features.summary: Writes the initial per-rank objects (and, for rank 0, the root) for a rank that never existed.
features.description: `boot_create` in one gather: `MDLog::create` (journal ino `0x200+r` in the metadata pool, header, JournalPointer `{front 0x200+r, back 0}`), an `ELid`; rank 0 only `create_empty_hierarchy` (root inode 1, mode 0755, uid/gid `mds_root_ino_uid/gid`, layout in the first data pool, root dirfrag `1.00000000` and inode `1.00000000.inode`, backtrace); `create_mydir_hierarchy` (mdsdir `0x100+r` with `stray0..stray9` at `0x600+10r+i`, mode 0500); `InoTable::reset` (free range `[(r+1)<<40, +2^40)`) and save; empty SessionMap save; `PurgeQueue::create`; rank 0 `SnapServer::reset` + save; then `ESubtreeMap`, flush, `wait_for_safe`, enable blocklist events. `creating_done` requests ACTIVE and syncs the snap client. If the creating holder dies, `FSMap::erase` forgets the rank and the next holder creates it again, rewriting the same objects without waiting for any blocklist epoch.
features.notes: The dirfrag commits set the header and the keys they hold; they do not clear unrelated omap keys of a recreated object (rank-lifecycle 3.7, derived from code). Object details: the root inode object is `1.00000000.inode` ("ceph fs volume v011" + InodeStore) with an explicit default layout on the first data pool and dl_dir_hash = mds_default_dir_hash; the root dirfrag is created empty and complete as a subtree root with dir_rep REP_ALL; each stray dirfrag and the mdsdir dirfrag are committed (the mdsdir has no backtrace) and the mdsdir inode is stored as `<0x100+r>.00000000.inode`. The monitor requires an empty metadata pool for `fs new` unless `--force`, so mkfs does not normally meet existing objects; `fs reset` marks old ranks stopped so their tables are reused. See also F-STORE-044 (journal creation), F-STORE-069 (InoTable), F-STORE-075 (SessionMap).

features.name: Restarting a stopped rank (up:starting)
features.summary: Brings back a rank that was cleanly stopped, appending to its capped journal without replay.
features.description: The monitor promotes a standby for the lowest rank in `stopped` when `in < max_mds` (also after `fs set down false`). Boot follows the starting column: tables load, the old journal (capped and trimmed by the stop) is not replayed, `MDLog::append` positions at its end and a new `ESubtreeMap` is journaled; `starting_done` requests ACTIVE and syncs the snap client. `active_start` then opens the root (non-zero ranks discover it from rank 0) and populates the mdsdir; `recovery_done` is not called. If the starting holder dies the rank returns to `stopped`.
features.notes: `up:starting` assumes a clean journal tail and does not wait for any blocklist epoch (rank-lifecycle gotchas 19, 26).

features.name: up:replay: journal replay of a failed rank
features.summary: The up:replay state: rebuilding the rank from its journal before any other recovery stage.
features.description: See F-STORE-037 (replay pipeline) and F-STORE-040 (replay errors). State-machine facts: up:replay starts after the fencing wait (F-CLU-037) and the boot stages (F-CLU-063); besides the cache, replay rebuilds sessions, completed request ids and created inos per session, completed cap flushes, in-progress truncates, inode ranges to purge, uncommitted leader and peer updates, ambiguous imports and fragment operations used by later phases; nothing is journaled during replay. After 30 s in up:replay the beacon carries MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME (F-ADM-081).

features.name: End of replay: journal reformat, writeable journal and the single-rank shortcut
features.summary: What happens when replay reaches the end of the journal and which state the rank asks for next.
features.description: `replay_done`: a follower schedules its next pass; otherwise it asserts `read_pos == write_pos`, rewrites the journal through `MDLog::reopen` if its stream format is older than `mds_journal_format`, makes the journal writeable, trims the tail, upgrades the snap table format on rank 0, applies dev wipe options, and requests `up:reconnect` directly when `get_num_in_mds() == 1 && get_num_failed_mds() == 0` ("i am alone", also starting a snap client sync), otherwise `up:resolve`.
features.notes: A damaged second rank keeps a file system out of the shortcut and also blocks resolve until `mds repaired` (rank-lifecycle gotcha 2).

legacy_parts.note: Journal reformat through MDLog::reopen when the stream format is older than mds_journal_format; the snap table format upgrade on rank 0. New journals are created in mds_journal_format (dev option, default 1 = JOURNAL_FORMAT_RESILIENT, present since v0.82), so the end-of-replay rewrite runs only for format-0 journals written by older C++ releases. SnapServer::upgrade_format() changes the table only when its version is 0 or snaprealm_v2_since is unset, which the decoder produces for struct_v < 5 tables written before v13.1.0. A snap table created at this commit gets version >= 1 and snaprealm_v2_since in reset_state.

features.name: Standby-replay follower loop
features.summary: A follower tails the active rank's journal every second to keep a warm cache for fast takeover.
features.description: Every `mds_replay_interval` (1 s) `standby_replay_restart` calls `Journaler::reread_head_and_probe` and then `_standby_replay_restart_finish`: if the active trimmed past what the follower had read (`old_read_pos < trimmed_pos`) it respawns; otherwise `standby_trim_segments` drops segments up to `expire_pos` (dirty objects marked clean without writing), trims the cache and replays the new events. The follower never journals, never opens the purge queue or the open file table, never talks to other ranks (messenger `mds.<gid>`), and its `inc` is 0. While a follower exists the active writes its journal without `FADVISE_DONTNEED`.
features.notes: Fragile: falling behind `trimmed_pos`, a journal rewrite or a missing object respawns the follower and loses its cache; a header re-read error other than `-EBLOCKLISTED` hits `ceph_assert` in `Journaler::_finish_reread_head_and_probe`; a corrupt event makes it report DAMAGED, which marks the rank damaged and blocklists the healthy active (rank-lifecycle gotcha 3). See also F-STORE-043 (journal side), F-CACHE-069 (cache maintenance).

features.name: Standby-replay takeover
features.summary: When the followed rank fails, the follower is promoted in place to `up:replay` and finishes replay from its warm cache.
features.description: `find_replacement_for` returns the follower (unless frozen) and `promote` switches it to `up:replay` and sets `inc`; the MDS only notes the change ("Monitor activated us! Deactivating replay loop"). The current pass (plus one more if its timer was armed) finishes; then `replay_done` starts the final pass: wait for OSDMap >= `last_failure_osd_epoch`, re-read the header and probe, open the purge queue, load the open file table, and replay the remaining events as a normal replay.

features.name: Recovery set and cluster-wide resolve/rejoin barriers
features.summary: Recovering ranks and survivors move through resolve and rejoin in lockstep, synchronised only through the published MDSMap.
features.description: The recovery set is `failed` + `damaged` + ranks in REPLAY..STOPPING, minus self (creating/starting ranks excluded), recomputed at `resolve_start` and at each new resolve round; a single-rank fs never computes it. Every rank evaluates on each map: when `is_resolving()` turns true (or a rank restarted), every rank >= RESOLVE runs `send_resolves`; when `is_rejoining()` turns true, every rank >= REJOIN runs `rejoin_send_rejoins`.
