Because the barriers require no rank in an earlier recovery state, the slowest replay gates everyone's resolve and every recovering rank's reconnect window (including its 45 s timeout) must end before any rejoin exchange. Resolve and rejoin have no timeouts; progress is driven only by messages, maps and IO.

features.name: Survivor reactions to a peer failing and recovering
features.summary: What still-active ranks do when another rank fails, while they keep serving their own subtrees.
features.description: Every rank >= RESOLVE that sees a peer newly down or restarted runs `handle_mds_failure(who)`: add it to `resolve_gather` and `rejoin_gather`, reset rejoin bookkeeping, notify the migrator and balancer, abort or keep in-flight peer and leader requests according to their 2PC state, retry requests waiting on it via `wait_for_active_peer`, cancel fragment operations that have not started refragmenting, kick `find_ino`/`open_ino` peers, and update snap table and scrub state. Operations needing the failed rank (remote auth pins, remote locks, witnesses) wait. When the peer reaches CLIENTREPLAY/ACTIVE/STOPPING (evaluated only on ranks that are themselves >= CLIENTREPLAY), `handle_mds_recovery` wakes waiters on its subtrees and `waiting_for_active_peer[who]`; ranks already >= REJOIN kick discovers and open_ino requests towards ranks newly >= REJOIN.
features.notes: An `OP_RENAMEPREP` from a failed srcdn auth is marked interrupted; the code comment says this "can cause mds to crash (does not affect integrity of FS)" (resolve-and-rejoin section 8).

features.name: Deferring messages to bootstrapping peers and dropping stale peer messages
features.summary: Inter-rank messaging rules around rank changes: queue messages for booting peers, piggyback maps, drop messages from old incarnations.
features.description: `send_message_mds(m, rank)` drops the message if the rank is not up, parks it in `waiting_for_bootstrapping_peer[rank]` while the peer is CREATING/STARTING/REPLAY (its messenger name changes when it leaves those states) and resends when its state is > REPLAY, and first sends the current `MMDSMap` when the peer's known epoch is older. Incoming messages from an MDS whose rank is down in the local map, or that did not arrive on the connection for the rank's current address, are dropped (`is_stale_message`), except MDSMaps and an `MCacheExpire` from a down rank still at its old address.
features.notes: See also F-ADM-004.

features.name: up:resolve entry and exit
features.summary: The multi-rank phase that settles everything left in doubt by the journals of the failed ranks.
features.description: `resolve_start` runs `reopen_log` (uncommitted fragment operations: finish those whose commit was journaled, roll back the others with `EFragment OP_ROLLBACK`), `calc_recovery_set`, `MDCache::resolve_start` (non-root ranks set the root dirfrag authority to unknown so rank 0 claims it; `resolve_gather = recovery_set`; snapshot of journaled snap-client tids) and wakes `waiting_for_resolve`. `maybe_resolve_finish` waits for a subtree resolve from every rank in `resolve_gather`, disambiguates imports, journals pending `ECommitted`, trims unlinked inodes, recomputes auth bits and completes `resolve_done`, which requests `up:reconnect` and starts a snap client sync. A single-rank fs skips this state; `reconnect_start` then runs `reopen_log` itself.

features.name: Subtree authority resolution (subtree resolves)
features.summary: Each rank claims the subtrees it owns so all ranks agree on authority after a failure.
features.description: After its peer resolves complete (and, on a survivor, a snap cache sync), each rank sends `MMDSResolve` (0x200) with `subtrees` (claimed dirfrags and bounds, nested own subtrees collapsed), `ambiguous_imports` and `table_clients` (snap tids) to every recovery-set rank (recovering sender) or to the ranks currently in RESOLVE (survivor); it is deferred while any migration is in flight. Receivers apply claims with `adjust_bounded_subtree_auth` (force-fragmenting missing bound dirfrags), remember others' ambiguous imports, update the snap client cache, and remove the sender from `resolve_gather`. A resolve received before this rank is in RESOLVE is retried at `resolve_start` if it wants RESOLVE, else dropped.
features.notes: The MDS-to-MDS protocol is free to redesign; only Rust ranks will speak it.

features.name: Ambiguous subtree import disambiguation
features.summary: Decides deterministically who owns a subtree whose migration was interrupted by a failure.
features.description: An import journaled (`EImportStart`) but not finished on a failed importer, or an import on a surviving importer in `IMPORT_ACKING` whose exporter failed, is ambiguous. A surviving importer reverses it if the exporter's resolve claims the subtree (no `EExport` on disk) and finishes it otherwise. A recovering importer, in `disambiguate_my_imports`, cancels and journals `EImportFinish(false)` if someone claimed it, else finishes it and journals `EImportFinish(true)`, then asserts no subtree is left with ambiguous authority. Migration protocol: [subtree-migration](../cpp-map/08-multi-mds/subtree-migration.md).
features.notes: See also F-MULTI-023 (migration side).

features.name: Cross-rank two-phase update outcomes (peer resolves and ECommitted)
features.summary: Settles link, unlink, rmdir and rename operations that spanned ranks when a participant failed.
features.description: The commit point is the leader's `EUpdate` (with `had_peers`) being durable. Recovering peers send `MMDSResolve` with `peer_requests` for every uncommitted `EPeerUpdate OP_PREPARE`; survivors send entries for prepared or committing peer requests whose leader is resolving. The leader answers `MMDSResolveAck` (0x201): COMMIT if it has the reqid in `uncommitted_leaders` (re-adding the peer so `ECommitted` waits for its `OP_COMMITTED`), ABORT otherwise (presumed abort); a survivor leader delays all answers while any listed `EUpdate` is still unsafe. A recovering peer journals `EPeerUpdate OP_COMMIT` and sends `OP_COMMITTED`, or rolls back from its saved rollback blob and journals `OP_ROLLBACK`. `finish_committed_leaders` journals `ECommitted` for leaders with no peers left. Unresolved entries pin both journals' tails.
features.notes: The `pending_leaders` gate is global: one unsafe leader update delays the peer resolves of every sender (resolve-and-rejoin section 6).

features.name: Rename-specific resolve handling
features.summary: Extra resolve rules for cross-rank renames: ambiguous witnesses and client caps of a renamed inode exported by a peer.
features.description: When the srcdn auth of a cross-rank rename fails while the leader is active, a surviving witness records an ambiguous peer update and sends a peer resolve to the active leader; on commit the entry is removed and the rename continues, on abort the rollback path preserves the peer request. A survivor peer that was exporting the renamed inode sends its current client caps (`peer_inode_cap`) instead of the committing flag; the leader (in RESOLVE) assigns each a new cap id (`++last_cap_id`, `issue_seq = 1`) in the ack and later sends `CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT` with an AUTH peer during rejoin. Rename protocol: [rename](../cpp-map/03-request-path/rename.md).

features.name: Snap table recovery and the SERVER_READY gate
features.summary: How snap-table recovery gates other ranks' recovery.
features.description: See F-STORE-082 for table 2PC recovery (finish_recovery, NOTIFY_PREP, AGREE re-sends, SERVER_READY). Recovery-state facts: the table server rank runs finish_recovery when it reaches up:resolve, and sends SERVER_READY to ranks newly reaching up:resolve; reconnect_gather_finish waits for the snap client to be synced before requesting up:rejoin, so a rank 0 failure during another rank's reconnect holds that rank in up:reconnect until the new rank 0 has recovered the table.

features.name: Post-resolve cache cleanup and authority bits
features.summary: After resolve the recovering rank drops orphaned inodes and recomputes which cached objects it is authoritative for.
features.description: `trim_unlinked_inodes` removes every non-base inode without a parent dentry (heartbeat reset every `mds_heartbeat_reset_grace` items). `recalc_auth_bits(false)` walks every subtree: objects in auth subtrees get AUTH; objects in non-auth subtrees lose AUTH and get REJOINING, dirfrags lose COMPLETE, empty non-subtree-root dirfrags are closed, inodes are marked clean (dirty parent and scatter state cleared except own subtree roots). A survivor instead may send pending rejoins. None of this runs for a single-rank file system.

features.name: up:reconnect: the client reconnect window and its timeout
features.summary: The window in which clients of the failed rank re-register their sessions, caps and locks before any request runs.
features.description: `reconnect_start` runs `reopen_log` if coming from replay, enables blocklist events and kills sessions whose address is blocklisted (raising the OSD epoch barrier if any), puts every open session in `client_reconnect_gather` with `last_cap_renew = now`, and wakes reconnects that arrived early. Clients act when the map shows the rank in `up:reconnect` (10). `reconnect_tick` (every 5 s tick, skipped while laggy) returns while blocklist evictions are pending or the gather is empty, and otherwise waits at least `mds_reconnect_timeout` (45 s) from `reconnect_start` and until neither a reconnect message nor any message from a not-yet-reconnected session arrived for `mds_reconnect_timeout`/2 (cap flushes and replayed requests sent ahead of the reconnect therefore extend the window; it has no upper bound while activity continues); then each missing client gets a cluster-log warning and is evicted (blocklisted with `mds_session_blocklist_on_timeout`, default true, after swapping `delegated_inos` and `free_prealloc_inos` so lost async creates are purged), except sessions whose metadata has a `timeout` key, which are kept for reclaim. The gather also finishes when every client reconnected or was closed; `reconnect_gather_finish` then waits for the snap client sync and requests `up:rejoin`.
features.notes: Message encoding and session states: [sessions](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/sessions.md). `reconnect_evicting` is never reset. Operators shorten the window by evicting clients listed by `session ls reconnecting=true`. With `mds_deny_all_reconnect` every reconnect is answered CLOSE; once every session left in the gather has been denied, `reconnect_tick` evicts them without waiting for the timeout or the activity extension. See also F-PROTO-057 (acceptance rules), F-PROTO-055 (client-side ordering), F-PROTO-056 (message encoding), F-CLU-096 (reclaim gating).

features.name: Recording caps and snaprealms from reconnect messages
features.summary: Turns each client's reconnect payload into the per-inode cap state that rejoin later matches and distributes.
features.description: For every part: `last_cap_renew = now`; each realm `{ino, seq, parent}` is recorded in `reconnected_snaprealms`; for each cap `last_cap_id` is raised to at least its `cap_id` and inodes being purged are skipped; an inode in cache and auth gets `CInode::reconnect_cap` (new cap keeps the client's `cap_id`, `wanted`, issued without revoke, `seq` reset) plus `add_reconnected_cap(realm_ino, snap_follows)`; an inode in cache but not auth goes to `cap_exports` for its authority (sent in the weak rejoin); an inode not in cache goes to `cap_imports` (resolved during rejoin). Dirty cap flushes with a new `client_tid` received during reconnect are OR-ed into `reconnected_caps[ino][client].dirty_caps` (snapflush flag for FLUSHSNAP). The client's parent ino + single-component name in each cap record is used later as an open hint.
features.notes: Cap semantics: [capabilities](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/capabilities.md).

features.name: Admission of replayed and retried requests during reconnect
features.summary: Requests that clients replay or resend after a failover are queued for ordered re-execution instead of waiting for `up:active`.
features.description: While in (or wanting) `up:reconnect`: a `CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_REQUEST` with `CEPH_MDS_FLAG_REPLAY` (1) or `CEPH_MDS_FLAG_ASYNC` (4) from an open session is marked `queued_for_replay` and appended to `replay_queue`; if `head.ino` is set and not already completed the ino is excluded from opening during rejoin (`add_replay_ino_alloc`). A retried request (`num_retry > 0`) is queued only if the session already has it in `completed_requests`, else it waits for active. Requests from missing or non-open sessions are dropped silently unless `mds_replay_unsafe_with_closed_session`. Session renewals are handled in any state; other session ops, reclaims, cap messages and cap releases wait for `up:clientreplay`; session close waits for active; other requests wait for active.
features.notes: With mds_replay_unsafe_with_closed_session a carried head.ino of a not-completed request is moved from the free to the delegated preallocation set so that it is not purged. Retried requests queued for replay lose their embedded cap releases. Requests re-sent during reconnect are not flagged REPLAY, only retried. Kernels send new requests only to ranks in up:active or later and libcephfs only to active or stopping ranks; libcephfs kick_requests at ACTIVE re-sends nothing in practice (derived from code). See also F-NS-002 (intake gating), F-CLU-095 (clientreplay).

features.name: Rejoin message exchange: weak rejoin, strong rejoin and acks
features.summary: Rebuilds replica lists, nonces and lock states between a recovering rank and every other rank.
features.description: `MMDSCacheRejoin` (0x202, v2) with op WEAK (1), STRONG (2) or ACK (3). A recovering rank sends WEAK to every recovery-set rank: weak dirfrags and dentries of the subtrees owned by the destination, dirty scatterlock data, root/mdsdir as weak inodes, and forwarded `cap_exports` with client instances and metadata. A survivor sends STRONG to each rank in REJOIN: replica nonces, lock states, `caps_wanted`, dentry linkage, plus its in-flight requests' remote auth pins, xlocks and wrlocks. Survivors answer WEAK immediately; a recovering rank sends its ACK (incremented nonces, `dirfrag_base`, `inode_base`, `inode_locks`, `imported_caps`) after its own gather finishes, built by walking every auth subtree. Survivors do not exchange rejoins with each other. There is no chunking: one message per rank pair of size proportional to the replicas.
features.notes: `up:rejoin` cannot be skipped (state graph). Survivors scan every inode in `inode_map` and `snap_inode_map` per weak rejoin (`rejoin_scour_survivor_replicas`) without heartbeat resets (resolve-and-rejoin section 3.20).

features.name: Recreating survivors' in-flight lock state on the recovering rank
features.summary: Strong rejoins carry the remote auth pins, xlocks and wrlocks that survivors' in-flight requests hold on the recovering rank's objects, so those requests can continue.
features.description: For each auth pin in a strong rejoin the recovering rank creates (or reuses) a peer `MDRequest` (`request_start_peer(reqid, attempt)`) that pins the object; an xlock takes the versionlock xlock locally, sets `LOCK_XLOCK` and `get_xlock`; a wrlock sets the lock to `LOCK_MIX` and `get_wrlock(true)`; frozen auth pins call `freeze_auth_pin`. Missing objects are invented. A strong rejoin arriving outside `rejoin` aborts the daemon unless it wants REJOIN.

features.name: Matching reconnected caps to inodes: OpenFileTable prefetch and open by number
features.summary: Finds the inode behind every cap a client reported that was not in cache after replay.
features.description: At rejoin start (once per daemon) the rank prefetches the OpenFileTable anchors (`mds<r>_openfiles.<i>`): directory inodes first (`open_ino` with the anchor chain as hint), optionally their dirfrags (`mds_oft_prefetch_dirfrags`), then file inodes; results naming another rank move caps to `cap_exports`, negatives go to `cap_imports_missing`. Remaining cap inodes are opened with `open_ino`: using the client's parent ino + single dentry name as a hint when present, otherwise asking peers in REJOIN or later and then reading the backtrace (`parent` xattr of `<ino>.00000000` in the default data pool, the backtrace's pool, then the metadata pool); dentry fetches are batched per dirfrag. Then `trim_non_auth` expires every unpinned non-auth dentry before weak rejoins are sent.
features.notes: See also F-STORE-089 (OpenFileTable prefetch).

features.name: Moving reconnected caps between ranks (IMPORT/EXPORT during rejoin)
features.summary: A cap a client reported to the wrong rank is moved to the inode's authority and the client is told with cap IMPORT and EXPORT messages.
features.description: The rank that received the reconnect forwards the cap in its weak rejoin. The authority installs it: a survivor only if the client already has a session with it (`rejoin_import_cap`), a recovering auth after force-opening sessions; a new cap keeps the client's `cap_id`, gets `seq` 1 and an incremented `mseq`, and the client receives `CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT` with peer `{old cap_id, 0, 0, old rank}`. The authority lists the result in its ack `imported_caps`; the forwarding rank then sends `CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT` (head cap_id = client's old id, peer = new cap or `mds = -1` to drop it). IMPORT and EXPORT come from different ranks in either order; the kernel and libcephfs match by `cap_id`.
features.notes: Forwarded caps for inodes a recovering auth cannot open are never answered: the forwarding rank sends no EXPORT and the client keeps a cap no rank tracks (resolve-and-rejoin section 8, derived from code). See also F-CAPS-036 (EXPORT/IMPORT messages).

features.name: Forced session open during rejoin
features.summary: Rejoin force-opens sessions for every client known from reconnect or from other ranks' weak rejoins.
features.description: See F-PROTO-041. Rejoin-specific: once per rejoin, if rejoin_client_map is non-empty, prepare_force_open_sessions runs for those clients and the rank journals ESessions and flushes; on safe the sessions moved to OPENING become OPEN and receive CEPH_SESSION_OPEN (cap auths, supported features and metric spec for Mimic+ clients, FORCE_RO if read-only). Even a single rank journals an ESessions whenever any client reconnected.

legacy_parts.note: The v1 CEPH_SESSION_OPEN without supported features or metric spec for sessions lacking CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8). Server::finish_force_open_sessions adds the supported-feature bitmap and metric spec only for sessions with CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8); for other sessions MClientSession falls back to a v1 message. The 7.3 kernel, both CentOS Stream samples and current libcephfs advertise bit 8; kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1 do not.

features.name: Choosing lock states from reconnected caps
features.summary: After rejoin the authority picks each inode lock's state from the caps clients hold, so caps and locks agree before serving.
features.description: `choose_lock_states_and_reconnect_caps` visits every head inode: re-marks dirty rstat, calls `CInode::choose_lock_states(issued | reconnected dirty caps)` and queues inodes with a snaprealm for reconciliation. For filelock, nestlock, dirfragtreelock, authlock, xattrlock and linklock on the auth (unless xlocked or MIX): EXCL if the lock's GEXCL|GBUFFER bits are issued or GWR with GCACHE|GSHARED, MIX if only GWR, else MIX (replicated) or LOCK (not replicated) if dirty, else SYNC; a loner is chosen when an EXCL/WR cap is issued.
features.notes: Lock state machines: [lock-types-and-state-machines](../cpp-map/05-locking/lock-types-and-state-machines.md).

features.name: Scatterlock recovery and NEED_RECOVER
features.summary: Rules that carry dirty scatter data (dirstat/rstat) across rejoin and keep requests off locks whose state may be stale until the cluster recovers.
features.description: Recovering replicas send scatterlock data for dirty subtree-root inodes in weak rejoins; survivors send their scatterlock state and dirty data in strong rejoins, and the recovering auth goes to MIX if any replica is in a MIX state. Acks re-send `inode_base` for every inode whose scatter content may have changed. The auth encodes MIX_SYNC/MIX_LOCK for replicas still in a gather and marks its lock NEED_RECOVER for MIX states; replica locks set from an ack are marked NEED_RECOVER always on a recovering rank and on a survivor unless previously SYNC. While the cluster is degraded, a non-replayed request needing an rdlock on a NEED_RECOVER lock drops its locks and waits for cluster recovery; `MLock` messages for objects still REJOINING are dropped.
features.notes: See also F-CAPS-090 (lock waits on a degraded cluster).

features.name: Snaprealm reconciliation and snapflush rebuild at the end of rejoin
features.summary: Rejoin step that catches clients up on snap realms and rebuilds owed snapshot flushes.
features.description: See F-SNAP-032. Recovery-specific: MDCache::open_snaprealms runs at the end of rejoin for the realms queued from reconnect messages; the first snapped inode of a cap whose snap_follows is older gets its locks set to LOCK_SNAP_SYNC with a wrlock until the owed flush arrives (rebuild_need_snapflush), and a FLUSHSNAP re-sent during reconnect marks the cap instead. Realms reported but not found are only logged. A survivor that sees a realm change in a rejoin ack sends SPLIT to clients with caps in the realm.
features.notes: See also F-CAPS-024 (FLUSHSNAP protocol), F-PROTO-061 (realm records in reconnect).

features.name: Rejoin cache repair: invented objects, stale fragmentation, missed link/unlink
features.summary: The authority fills gaps in its cache with placeholder objects fetched from RADOS and repairs replicas whose structure diverged.
features.description: Objects named in strong rejoins but absent locally are invented (`REJOINUNDEF` inode with only its number, or frag `*` dirfrag with the default hash) and fetched top-down from their parent dirfrags before the gather finishes (`open_undef_inodes_dirfrags`). Survivors' dirfrags that do not match the auth's fragtree are mapped onto local leaves, and the replica refragments from the ack. A survivor whose primary linkage differs from the auth's missed an `MDentryLink`/`MDentryUnlink`; the auth re-replicates the inode's new location in its ack and the replica repairs its linkage in `handle_cache_rejoin_ack`. Snapshot dentries are trimmed from strong rejoins.
features.notes: Inconsistencies are handled by `ceph_assert` rather than repair in several places (non-empty `isolated_inodes` after an ack, dir hash mismatch for an opened undefined directory, unexpected states in `rejoin_open_ino_finish`) (resolve-and-rejoin section 8).

features.name: Rejoin on a single-rank file system
features.summary: With one rank, rejoin runs without messages but still pays the full cap-matching and cache-scan cost before serving.
features.description: For `max_mds = 1`: resolve is skipped, the recovery set is empty, and no `disambiguate_my_imports`, `finish_committed_leaders`, `trim_unlinked_inodes` or `recalc_auth_bits(false)` runs. Rejoin still performs the OpenFileTable prefetch, `open_ino` of every reconnected cap inode not in cache, `trim_non_auth`, forced session opens (an `ESessions` event if any client reconnected), cap reconnect, lock state choice, file recovery identification and `open_snaprealms` (client `MClientSnap` messages) before `rejoin_done`.

features.name: up:clientreplay: ordered re-execution of replayed requests
features.summary: Re-executes, one at a time in arrival order, requests whose unsafe replies clients already saw, before any new request is served.
features.description: `rejoin_done` requests CLIENTREPLAY if `replay_queue` is non-empty or reclaims are pending, else ACTIVE (or STOPPED with no subtrees). `clientreplay_start` wakes `waiting_for_replay` and `queue_one_replay` moves the head of `replay_queue` to the finished queue; the next one is queued only when the current request reaches journal submission (replays never get an early reply), is cleaned up, or is dropped as already completed (a reply with the created ino in `extra_bl`) or duplicate. Replays skip the wait-for-cluster-recovery lock paths, reuse the client's reconnected cap for inodes they create, bypass QoS, and are logged as "failed to replay" on error. When the queue is empty and the reclaim gather is empty, the journal is made safe and ACTIVE is requested.
features.notes: Completed-request detection per session belongs to [request-lifecycle](../cpp-map/03-request-path/request-lifecycle.md). Possible stall by code reading: a replayed request already completed whose session is not open returns before `queue_one_replay` (rank-lifecycle gotcha 10, unverified at runtime). See also F-NS-013 (handler-side rules), F-CAPS-059 (creates).

features.name: Reclaim gating of the clientreplay to active transition
features.summary: Sessions of NFS-Ganesha instances that did not reconnect hold the whole rank in `up:clientreplay` until reclaimed, closed or autoclosed.
features.description: At reconnect timeout, missing sessions whose metadata has a `timeout` key (set by `ceph_set_session_timeout`, used by Ganesha) are kept in `client_reclaim_gather` instead of being evicted. A restarted instance opens a new session (allowed from clientreplay) and sends `CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_RECLAIM` with `CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET` and the same `uuid` (same auth name or EPERM); the old session is then killed or evicted with blocklisting. `maybe_clientreplay_done` requires the reclaim gather to be empty. With defaults a never-reclaimed session is evicted by `find_idle_sessions` after `session_autoclose` (300 s) from `last_cap_renew`, so the rank may stay in `up:clientreplay`, serving no new requests, for about 300 s; the `timeout` value is not consulted.
features.notes: Reclaim message semantics: [libcephfs-fuse-ganesha-expectations](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/libcephfs-fuse-ganesha-expectations.md). `rejoin_done` requests up:clientreplay instead of up:active while the reclaim gather is non-empty, and a close of such a session (by reclaim or kill) removes it from the gather. REQUEST_CLOSE waits for up:active, so a client closing sessions while a rank is held in up:clientreplay times out. A Ganesha restart that takes longer than session_autoclose loses the old session to eviction (blocklisted by default) rather than to reclaim. See also F-PROTO-063 (reclaim protocol), F-PROTO-046 (timeout key).

features.name: Activation (recovery_done and active_start)
features.summary: The work a rank does when it enters `up:clientreplay` or `up:active`, before and as it starts serving new requests.
features.description: `recovery_done` (from REJOIN) starts recovered truncates, orphan inode purges and file size recovery, then `populate_mydir`: fetch the mdsdir dirfrag and the header of each stray dirfrag, recreate missing `stray<i>` dentries via a journaled `EUpdate`, pin the strays, mark the cache open (all requests wait for it) and activate the stray manager and purge queue. `active_start` sets the active flag (QoS on), opens the root for CREATING/STARTING, registers the metrics handler (and the metric aggregator on rank 0), cleans per-segment open-file lists, handles leftover cap imports, wakes `waiting_for_replay`, reissues caps, wakes `waiting_for_active` (all requests and session closes that waited) and sets up the quiesce agent. From then on every map raises the OSD epoch barrier.
features.notes: Stray handling belongs to [strays-and-purge](../cpp-map/11-background-services/strays-and-purge.md). The "fragment was unreadable, recreating it now" branch of `populate_mydir` appears unreachable because `CDir::go_bad` never leaves version 0 (rank-lifecycle gotcha 31, derived from code). See also F-BG-021 (stray scan at activation).

legacy_parts.note: The 'fragment was unreadable, recreating it now' branch of MDCache::populate_mydir. The 'fragment ... was unreadable, recreating it now' branch of populate_mydir requires an mdsdir dirfrag with fnode version 0 and STATE_BADFRAG. The only setter of STATE_BADFRAG in src/mds is CDir::go_bad, which with complete=true first sets a version-0 fnode to version 1, and Migrator::export_dir refuses system directories, so the state cannot arrive with an import either.

features.name: Leftover reconnect caps and cap reissue at activation
features.summary: Caps whose inode was never found are answered with a stale EXPORT, and all caps are re-evaluated before serving.
features.description: `export_remaining_imported_caps` sends, for each leftover `cap_imports` ino and client with a session, `MClientCaps(CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT, ino, realm 0, cap_id 0, mseq 0, osd_epoch_barrier)` with peer `{0, 0, 0, -1, 0}`, logs clog WARN "failed to reconnect caps for missing inodes:" and wakes cap-reconnect waiters. `reissue_all_caps` runs `Locker::eval` or `issue_caps` on every head inode with caps (frozen inodes deferred), which may grant or revoke caps with the current OSD epoch barrier.
features.notes: The stale EXPORT has `head.cap_id = 0`; both the kernel (`cap->cap_id != ex->cap_id`) and libcephfs ignore it, so clients keep caps for inodes the MDS no longer tracks and only the clog warning remains (resolve-and-rejoin section 8, derived from code).

features.name: File size and mtime recovery for writers that did not come back
features.summary: Recovery side of file size and mtime recovery for writers that did not reconnect.
features.description: See F-CAPS-022. Recovery-specific: granted writeable ranges are journaled in inode_t::client_ranges. At the end of rejoin identify_files_to_recover puts every auth head regular file with a range whose client has no cap in rejoin_recover_q (filelock LOCK_PRE_SCAN) and every other one in rejoin_check_q; after activation start_files_to_recover moves the first set to LOCK_SCAN through file_recover (no rdlock, wrlock, xlock, lease or file caps, so stat/read/write block) and hands them to the RecoveryQueue.
features.notes: Possible auth-pin leak when an inode is re-enqueued while a probe restarts (rank-lifecycle section 4, derived from code). `identify_files_to_recover` stops marking caps clientwriteable at the first client without a cap (gotcha 15).

features.name: Re-executing interrupted truncates after recovery
features.summary: Recovery side of data-object truncation: truncates interrupted by a failover are re-run.
features.description: See F-STORE-065. Recovery-specific: replay rebuilds per-segment truncating_inodes from EMetaBlob truncate_start/truncate_finish; start_recovered_truncates (from recovery_done) auth-pins each inode and re-runs _truncate_inode. Inodes owing a snapshot flush with Fb issued first move their filelock to LOCK_XLOCKSNAP. Recovered truncates do not re-send CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC; re-execution is idempotent at the OSD through truncate_seq.
features.notes: Truncate completions `ceph_assert(r == 0 || r == -ENOENT)` (rank-lifecycle gotcha 16). See also F-NS-062 (truncate request).

features.name: Purging orphaned preallocated and delegated inodes
features.summary: Recovery side of the purge of preallocated and delegated inode numbers whose session closed or was lost.
features.description: See F-STORE-072. Recovery-specific: purges recorded by ESession events replayed before activation start from recovery_done (MDCache::start_purge_inodes); purges of sessions closed in clientreplay, active or stopping start immediately. At the end of the reconnect window each session that is evicted (not kept for reclaim) first has delegated_inos and free_prealloc_inos swapped, so after a restart (delegated_inos empty, free_prealloc_inos = prealloc_inos) every unused preallocated number of a client that did not come back is purged rather than released.
features.notes: Only object 0 is removed (code FIXME "handle non-default data pool and namespace"), so larger orphaned async-created files leak data objects (rank-lifecycle gotcha 12).

features.name: Stopping a rank (up:stopping to down:stopped)
features.summary: The orderly drain a rank performs when the monitor shrinks the file system.
features.description: `stopping_start` disables QoS and calls `shutdown_start`. While stopping, client requests are still processed and forwarded as subtrees leave; new session opens are dropped silently. Each 5 s tick runs `shutdown_pass` until all hold: non-zero ranks export strays to rank 0 (at most 100 in flight) and every auth non-mdsdir subtree to its parent's authority (rank 0 if that is not active), ignoring pins when `max_mds == 0`; the cache is trimmed; remaining sessions get `terminate_sessions` (`CEPH_SESSION_CLOSE`); the journal is trimmed to one segment and capped with an `ELid`; no Objecter op is in flight. Then the purge queue is drained (clog "waiting for purge queue" each tick) and `stopping_done` requests `down:stopped`. The capped journal, tables and mdsdir stay in RADOS for a later `up:starting`.
features.notes: If the stopping holder dies after capping its journal, the replacement replays only the `ELid`, finds no subtrees and completes the stop through `REJOIN -> STOPPED` (rank 0 with more than one replayed event is marked damaged instead) (rank-lifecycle 3.13, derived from code). See also F-PROTO-054 (session termination and last-rank eviction), F-BG-022 (stray export), F-BG-023 (purge queue drain), F-MULTI-049 (subtree hand-off), F-STORE-021 (journal capping).

features.name: Reporting a rank as DAMAGED
features.summary: When a rank's metadata cannot be loaded or replayed, the MDS reports DAMAGED so no daemon is assigned to it until an operator repairs it.
features.description: `MDSRank::damaged()` sets `want_state = down:damaged`, flushes the cluster log, refreshes health, sends a beacon and waits up to 0.95 x `mds_mon_shutdown_timeout` (5 s) for the ack **while holding `mds_lock`**, then respawns even without an ack. Triggers: table, sessionmap, journal pointer or header read/decode errors; `boot_start` `-EINVAL`/`-ENOENT`; `validate_sessions` inconsistency; corrupt or unbounded journal events or a missing journal object; unhandled journal write errors; rank 0 with more than one journal event but no subtrees after rejoin; failure to open the root or mdsdir inode/dirfrag or a stray dirfrag; a file size probe OSD error; `mds_standby_replay_damaged` (dev). The monitor side is described under "Damaged ranks and mds repaired".
features.notes: If `damaged()` runs on the dispatch thread, or while it is blocked on `mds_lock`, the beacon ack cannot be processed and the wait times out; the code comment accepts that the monitor may miss the report (process-and-threading section 8). See also F-STORE-040 (replay errors), F-BG-057 (fatal damage), F-CLU-049 (monitor side).

features.name: Respawn: re-exec as a fresh standby
features.summary: The C++ MDS discards its identity by re-executing itself whenever it may no longer act for its rank.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::respawn` dumps the recent in-memory log and `execv`s `/proc/self/exe` with the original arguments (same PID; `_exit(0)` with `mds_valgrind_exit`); the new process gets a new messenger nonce, mon session and gid and boots as a standby; its boot beacon fails the old gid through unique-name enforcement. Triggers: removed from the MDSMap (failed by the monitor, or after `down:stopped`); a different rank or an invalid transition in a map; any `MDSIOContextBase` completion with `-EBLOCKLISTED` or `-ETIMEDOUT`; journal write `-EBLOCKLISTED`; standby-replay `-EAGAIN` or falling behind `trimmed_pos`; `damaged()`; asok/tell `respawn` (after 1 s).
features.notes: Because respawn keeps the PID, a supervisor (systemd, cephadm, Rook) does not observe a process exit (process-and-threading section 7, inferred from exec semantics). `MDLog::_recovery_thread` calls `respawn()` on `-EBLOCKLISTED` without holding `mds_lock`. See also F-STORE-095 (fenced respawn path), F-ADM-033 (respawn command).

features.name: Suicide and orderly shutdown
features.summary: Process exit paths: signals, asok `exit`, fatal boot errors and unwritable compat.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::suicide` (must hold `mds_lock`): set `stopping`, cancel the tick, unregister asok commands, send the DNE beacon (lock released, up to ~1 s), stop the beacon thread and MgrClient, then `MDSRankDispatcher::shutdown` (timer, MDLog threads, purge queue, metrics, finisher stopped without flushing pending contexts, Objecter, MonClient, progress thread, messenger) or, without a rank, timer/MonClient/messenger; `main` returns from `msgr->wait()` and deletes the daemon only on a clean shutdown (no rank, or rank in `stopped`). Triggers: SIGINT/SIGTERM, asok/tell `exit` (after 1 s), MonClient init/auth/rotating-key failure, an MDSMap compat the daemon cannot write, an unexpected `boot_start` error (including `-EAGAIN` outside standby-replay).
features.notes: Possible shutdown deadlocks by code reading: `suicide()` unregisters asok hooks while holding `mds_lock` while hooks block on it; shutdown joins `mds-metrics`/`mds-ping` under `mds_lock`; `PurgeQueue::shutdown` joins its finisher under its lock. Between `MDSDaemon::stopping` and `MDSRank::stopping` (about 1 s) IO completions and timers still mutate state (process-and-threading section 8).

features.name: Write error policy
features.summary: Failure exits triggered by RADOS write errors.
features.description: See F-STORE-100 (metadata write errors: ignore, read-only or respawn per mds_action_on_write_error) and F-STORE-015 (journal write errors: damaged). Failure-exit view: -EBLOCKLISTED always respawns (F-CLU-105); mds_action_on_write_error 2 or more respawns (the log says "suicide"); journal write errors other than -EBLOCKLISTED mark the rank damaged (F-CLU-104).

features.name: Process bootstrap (ceph-mds -i <id>)
features.summary: How one `ceph-mds` process starts: arguments, identity, messenger, MonClient and the main wait.
features.description: `main`: `global_init` as an MDS daemon; optional CPU pinning to `mds_numa_node`; only the obsolete `--hot-standby <x>` extra argument is accepted; the id must be given and must not be empty or start with a digit; `pick_addresses(PUBLIC)`; optional fork/daemonize; one messenger `mds.-1` with a random nonce, cluster protocol 36; a 2-thread asio pool; `MonClient`; `MDSDaemon::init`; one-shot SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers (SIGHUP reopens logs); the main thread blocks in `msgr->wait()` until shutdown. `MDSDaemon::init` registers dispatchers, authenticates, waits for rotating keys (`rotating_keys_bootstrap_timeout` 30 s, up to `max_rotating_auth_attempts` 10, else suicide `-ETIMEDOUT`), subscribes `mdsmap` from epoch 0, sets up the admin socket, starts the timer and the beacon (`want_state = up:boot`) and the 5 s tick.

legacy_parts.note: The obsolete `--hot-standby` argument; cluster protocol 36, which only msgr1 handshakes carry. main() accepts `--hot-standby <x>` only to log '--hot-standby is obsolete and has no effect', and cephadm, Rook and the mgr modules never pass it (grep). The cluster protocol 36 set with set_cluster_protocol is read only by AsyncMessenger::get_proto_version, which only ProtocolV1 (msgr1) calls; msgr2 connections carry no protocol number.

features.name: Single public messenger with per-peer-type policies
features.summary: One messenger and one address vector serve clients, monitors, OSDs, mgr and peer MDSs.
features.description: The MDS creates one async messenger (`ms_public_type` or `ms_type`), so the address vector the monitor records from beacons is the one clients and peers connect to. Policies: default (OSD, mgr) `lossy_client` requiring OSDREPLYMUX; MON `lossy_client` requiring UID|PGID64; MDS `lossless_peer` requiring UID; CLIENT `stateful_server` (lossless, server, standby, reset check) requiring nothing. No byte or message throttlers are attached to policies; inbound backpressure is the global `ms_dispatch_throttle_bytes` (100 MiB). msgr v1 handshakes use protocol 32 for clients and 36 between MDSs.
features.notes: Transport and authentication as clients see them: [transport-auth-and-client-library-contract](../cpp-map/00-architecture/transport-auth-and-client-library-contract.md) and [wire-protocol](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/wire-protocol.md). See also F-PROTO-006 (client policy), F-PROTO-107 (peer-MDS policy), F-PROTO-008 (entity name).

legacy_parts.note: msgr v1 handshake protocol numbers (32 for clients, 36 between MDSs). The protocol numbers 32 and 36 are exchanged only in msgr1 connect and connect-reply messages, and the 7.3 kernel sends CEPH_MDSC_PROTOCOL only from messenger_v1.c. Baseline clients use msgr2: the kernel through the ms_mode=prefer-crc that mount.ceph adds, libcephfs by connecting to the first usable address of the vector, which daemons list as v2 before v1. The per-peer-type policies and required features are also enforced on msgr2 connections.

features.name: MonClient session, keys and subscriptions
features.summary: The MDS's monitor session: authentication, service keys and the maps it subscribes to.
features.description: The MonClient wants service keys for MON, OSD, MDS and MGR and acts as the messenger's auth client and server (cephx verification of clients happens on messenger threads). Subscriptions: `monmap` and `config` (from `authenticate`, so `mds_join_fs` and other options can come from the mon config database), `mdsmap` from epoch 0 (`MDSDaemon::init`), `mgrmap` when the daemon first appears in an FSMap (starting the MgrClient), `osdmap` through the Objecter (plus `MMonGetVersion` for `wait_for_latest_osdmap`). Mon caps needed (all in `profile mds`): `mds` all, `mon r`, `osd r`, `osd pool rmsnap`, `osd blocklist`, `log w`, config-key under `daemon-private/mds.<id>/`. A `MSG_MON_COMMAND` from a monitor is dropped with a clog warning.
features.notes: See also F-PROTO-103 (MonClient protocol duties).

legacy_parts.note: Discarding MSG_MON_COMMAND (MMonCommand) from pre-Luminous monitors. MDSDaemon::handle_core_message discards a MSG_MON_COMMAND from a monitor with the clog warning 'dropping `mds tell` command from legacy monitor'. Monitors up to v11.x forwarded `mds tell` to MDS daemons as MMonCommand; the MDS-side handling was removed in v12.0.2 (commit 2be6297d12e). No monitor code at this commit sends MMonCommand to an MDS: the only constructions are MonClient requests to monitors and an OSDMonitor-internal retry.

features.name: Global mds_lock (FIFO fair mutex)
features.summary: The single process-wide lock that serialises every metadata and rank-state change in the C++ MDS.
features.description: `mds_lock` is a `ceph::fair_mutex` (FIFO ticket lock: strict arrival-order hand-off, every unlock wakes all waiters, not recursive, no lockdep). It is taken by the dispatch thread for every message reaching `MDSDaemon`, by the timer thread for every callback, by the rank finisher for IO completions, by the progress thread, the log-trim, cache-trim and log-replay threads, admin commands, signal handling and several subsystem callbacks. Rule: whoever takes it must check `stopping` and either do nothing or never release it. Lock-held assertions are compiled only in debug builds. Details: [mds_lock-analysis](../cpp-map/00-architecture/mds_lock-analysis.md).

features.name: Completion contexts and the rank finisher
features.summary: How asynchronous IO and journal completions re-enter the locked world in the C++ MDS.
features.description: `MDSContext` completions assert `mds_lock` and reset the heartbeat; `MDSIOContextBase::complete` takes `mds_lock` itself, drops the completion if the rank is stopping, respawns on `-EBLOCKLISTED`/`-ETIMEDOUT`, and is tracked in a global list used for `MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO`; `MDSLogContextBase` also advances the journal safe position; `C_IO_Wrapper` re-queues on the finisher; `MDSGather` fans in. Objecter callbacks are wrapped in `C_OnFinisher` so they run one at a time on the `mds-rank-fin` thread; Journaler callbacks likewise, so journal commits complete in order.
features.notes: `queue_waiters` completes every context with 0, losing the waker's error code; once stopping, `MDSIOContextBase::complete` silently leaks contexts (process-and-threading section 8). See also F-STORE-011 (ordered journal completions).

features.name: Progress thread and rank waiter queues
features.summary: Per-rank queues where messages and requests park until a state, peer, map epoch or lagginess condition changes.
features.description: Queues under `mds_lock`: `finished_queue` (contexts drained by `_advance_queues` at the end of each top-level dispatch or by the `mds-rank-progr` thread), `waiting_for_nolaggy` (deferred messages), `waiting_for_active`, `waiting_for_replay`, `waiting_for_resolve/_reconnect/_rejoin`, `waiting_for_active_peer[rank]` (`MDS_RANK_NONE` = cluster recovered), `waiting_for_bootstrapping_peer[rank]`, `waiting_for_mdsmap[epoch]`, `replay_queue`. Parked messages are re-dispatched with `C_MDS_RetryMessage` and re-run all checks, so per-connection processing order is not strict after parking.

features.name: Dispatcher chain, message priorities and ordering
features.summary: The order in which incoming messages reach the MDS and which ones bypass `mds_lock`.
features.description: After decoding, OSD replies and watch-notify are fast-dispatched into the Objecter on messenger threads; everything else goes to one `ms_dispatch` thread through a priority queue (priority >= 64 strict, round-robin per connection within a priority). Dispatcher order: MonClient, Beacon (acks), MetricsHandler (client metrics, pings; after activation), MgrClient, Objecter (OSD maps acknowledged and passed on), MetricAggregator (rank 0), then `MDSDaemon` (takes `mds_lock`). Clients send at priority 127 (libcephfs metrics at 195); connection events are queued at 255 and overtake messages already queued for that connection. Debug hooks (`mds_thrash_exports`, `mds_thrash_fragments`) and `update_mlogger` run at the end of each top-level dispatch.

features.name: Rank message validation and routing
features.summary: Which message types a rank accepts, from which peer types, and which subsystem handles them.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::ms_dispatch2` handles core messages itself (MDSMap, OSDMap, `MRemoveSnaps`, `MCommand`, MonMap; legacy `MMonCommand` dropped) and filters by peer type. `MDSRankDispatcher::ms_dispatch` asserts that any message from an MDS is an `MMDSOp` and updates the client session's `last_seen`. `_dispatch` runs quiesce-DB messages first, drops stale peer messages, accepts only a whitelist (ports 0x2xx cache, 0x4xx migrator, client session/reconnect/reclaim/request/reply, peer request, heartbeat, table request, lock, inode file caps, scrub, client caps/caprelease/lease) and routes them to MDCache, Migrator, Server, MDBalancer, table client/server, Locker or ScrubStack. Rank-state gating is done by each subsystem, not centrally.
features.notes: `MSG_REMOVE_SNAPS` dereferences `mds_rank` without a null check; any non-`MMDSOp` message from an MDS peer that reaches rank dispatch aborts the daemon (process-and-threading section 8). See also F-ADM-004 (security view), F-PROTO-017 (client message catalog).

legacy_parts.note: Discarding MSG_MON_COMMAND (MMonCommand) from pre-Luminous monitors. MDSDaemon::handle_core_message discards MSG_MON_COMMAND from monitors with a clog warning; only monitors up to v11.x sent it (forwarded `mds tell`), and no monitor code at this commit sends MMonCommand to an MDS. MRemoveSnaps, MCommand, MDSMap, OSDMap and MonMap handling are current (the current monitor replies MRemoveSnaps to SERVER_OCTOPUS peers).

features.name: Outbound messaging helpers and local delivery
features.summary: The send paths a rank uses for clients and peers, including counted pushes and self-addressed messages.
features.description: `send_message_mds(m, rank)` (drop if not up, defer to bootstrapping peers, piggyback a newer MDSMap) and an address-based variant without checks; `forward_message_mds` never forwards a client request between MDSs but sends the client `MClientRequestForward(dest, num_fwd+1, client_must_resend=true)`; `send_message_client_counted` increments the session `cap_push_seq` (a client close is honoured only if its seq matches) and queues on `preopen_out_queue` when there is no connection. Messages to self go through the messenger's local delivery thread and are processed later on `ms_dispatch`.
features.notes: Request forwarding and push-sequence semantics as clients see them belong to [request-lifecycle](../cpp-map/03-request-path/request-lifecycle.md) and [sessions](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/sessions.md).

features.name: Tick and the shared timer
features.summary: The periodic upkeep of a rank and the timer that runs all periodic callbacks under `mds_lock`.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::tick` runs every `mds_tick_interval` (5 s) on the shared `SafeTimer`, which holds `mds_lock` while running every callback. `MDSRankDispatcher::tick`: heartbeat reset; return if laggy; slow-op scan; wake the progress thread; flush the journal; in clientreplay/active/stopping clear laggy clients, find idle sessions, evict cap-revoke non-responders and run `Locker::tick`; in reconnect `reconnect_tick`; in active the balancer, stale freeze detection, snap server OSD check and scrub status (rank 0); in active/stopping `update_targets`; in stopping `shutdown_pass` and the purge-queue drain; finally `notify_health`. Other timer users: task status (2 s), standby-replay restart (1 s), retry timers of several subsystems.

features.name: Thread inventory of the daemon and its subsystems
features.summary: The threads one C++ MDS process runs and which of them take `mds_lock`.
features.description: Without `mds_lock`: `msgr-worker-N` (3), `ms_local`, `io_context_pool` (2), MonClient/MgrClient/Objecter timers, `mds-beacon`, `log`, `service` (touches `heartbeat_file` when healthy), `mds-log-submit`, `mds-pq-fin` and the PurgeQueue timer, `mds-ping`. With `mds_lock`: `ms_dispatch`, `safe_timer`, `admin_socket` (most commands), `signal_handler`, `mds-rank-fin`, `mds-rank-progr`, `mds-log-trim` (every 1 s while active/stopping), `mds-cache-trim` (every 1 s, heap release every 10 s), `mds-log-replay` (per event), `mds-log-recvr`/`-reopen` (briefly), `mds-metrics`, `mds-q-db`, `mds-q-agt`, dmClock threads. Process-global object counters and the IO context list make "one rank per process" an implicit assumption.

features.name: MDS-originated client requests (MDSMetaRequest)
features.summary: Internal operations a rank performs by sending `MClientRequest`s to another rank.
features.description: `issue_tid()` hands out per-process tids for internal requests (`reqid = mds.<rank>:<tid>`). Stray reintegration and migration send `MClientRequest(CEPH_MDS_OP_RENAME)` to another MDS and remember it in `internal_client_requests[tid]` (pinning the dentry with `PIN_PURGING`); the peer's safe `MClientReply` erases the entry. `Server::create_quota_realm` sends a fire-and-forget `SETXATTR ceph.quota` to the auth rank; its reply only logs "no pending request".
